cmd:appearance.addFill.label: Add New Fill

cmd:appearance.addStroke.label: Add New Stroke
cmd:appearance.addStroke.params: {ids?, target?} add a stroke on top of each selected object's own stack (a copy of its top stroke, else the default stroke)

cmd:appearance.clear.label: Clear Appearance
cmd:appearance.clear.params: {ids?, target?} leave each object one empty fill and stroke (None; a group none of its own) and reset its opacity and blend mode
cmd:appearance.clear.desc: Leave each selected object one empty fill and stroke and reset its opacity and blend mode.

cmd:appearance.copyFrom.label: Eyedropper
cmd:appearance.copyFrom.params: {source: id, ids?, pickUp?, apply? (trees as eyedropper.setOptions, merged over the Eyedropper Options for this call), reverse?: bool, append?: bool} copy the attributes both picked up and applied (by default the whole appearance stack, opacity and blend mode, and from type to type the character and paragraph attributes) from `source` to ids (default: the selection), the fill, stroke and weight also to the paint defaults; `reverse` (Alt-click) copies from the first selected object (or ids) onto `source` instead; `append` (Shift+Alt-click) adds the source's fills, strokes and effects on top of each target's stack; placed gradients land at the same place relative to each target's bounds (defaults: fitted to new art) → {ids}

cmd:appearance.duplicateItem.label: Duplicate Item
cmd:appearance.duplicateItem.params: {index | indices: [..] (paint-order item indices), to?: paint-order index of the copy (one `index` only; default: right above it, as Alt-dragging a row places it), ids?, target?} copy fills/strokes with their effects
cmd:appearance.duplicateItem.desc: Duplicate a fill or stroke row, with its effects, in the selected objects' appearance stacks.

cmd:appearance.moveItem.label: Reorder Appearance Item
cmd:appearance.moveItem.params: {from: paint-order item index | "contents", to, contents?: count, ids?, target?} move fill/stroke `from` to paint-order index `to`; on a group, layer or type the Contents (Characters) row stays between the same items (a moved item landing next to it keeps its side) unless `contents` says how many items paint below it afterwards. from "contents": move that row so `to` items paint below the members (characters) and the rest above → {index: where the item landed | contents: the row's slot}
cmd:appearance.moveItem.desc: Move a fill or stroke to another position in an object's paint order.

cmd:appearance.newArt.label: New Art Appearance
cmd:appearance.newArt.params: {} what the next object drawn gets → {basic: New Art Has Basic Appearance, appearance: {items, effects} (the model's JSON; placed gradients relative to the unit box), opacity: 0..100, blend, graphicStyle: the style it is linked to or null, inherited: taken from the last selection}
cmd:appearance.newArt.desc: Report the fill, stroke, effects, opacity and blend mode that new art will get.

cmd:appearance.reduceToBasic.label: Reduce to Basic Appearance
cmd:appearance.reduceToBasic.params: {ids?, target?} keep only the topmost visible fill and stroke, without their own opacity, blend mode or effects (a group keeps no rows it lacked), and drop the object's effects
cmd:appearance.reduceToBasic.desc: Reduce each selected object to one basic fill and stroke, dropping extra items, effects, opacity and blend mode.

cmd:appearance.removeItem.label: Remove Item
cmd:appearance.removeItem.params: {index | indices: [..] (paint-order item indices), ids?, target?} remove those fills/strokes from each target object's own stack
cmd:appearance.removeItem.desc: Remove chosen fills or strokes from the selected objects' appearance stacks.

cmd:appearance.setActiveItem.params: {index: paint-order item index in the first selected object's stack | null} make that fill/stroke row the target of the paint.setFill/setStroke, stroke.set/setAdvanced, paint.editGradient/setGradientGeom, transparency.set and effect.* calls that omit `item` (a fill row brings the Fill proxy forward, a stroke row the Stroke proxy); null or any selection change clears it → {index}
cmd:appearance.setActiveItem.desc: Choose the appearance row that later paint, transparency and effect commands act on.

cmd:appearance.setItem.label: Appearance Item
cmd:appearance.setItem.params: {index: paint-order item index, ids? (default: the selection), target?: "object"|"contents", opacity?: 0..100, blend?: name, visible?: bool, weight?: pt (strokes), color?|none?|swatch?|gradient? (as paint.setFill)} edit one fill/stroke of each target object's own appearance stack
cmd:appearance.setItem.desc: Edit one fill or stroke of the selected objects: colour, opacity, blend mode, visibility or weight.

cmd:appearance.setNewArtBasic.label: New Art Has Basic Appearance
cmd:appearance.setNewArtBasic.params: {on?: bool (omitted: toggle)} the Appearance panel option (the preference newArtBasic, on by default): on, new art takes one fill and stroke (with the Stroke panel's options); off, the whole appearance of the last selected object (every fill, stroke and effect, opacity and blend mode) → {on}
cmd:appearance.setNewArtBasic.desc: Toggle whether new objects get a basic fill and stroke or the last selected object's whole appearance.

cmd:appearance.showAllHidden.label: Show All Hidden Attributes
cmd:appearance.showAllHidden.params: {ids?, target?} make every hidden fill, stroke and effect (the object's and each item's) of each selected object visible again; errors when nothing is hidden → {ids}
cmd:appearance.showAllHidden.desc: Make every hidden fill, stroke and effect of the selected objects visible again.

cmd:appearance.targetContents.label: Target Contents
cmd:appearance.targetContents.params: {ids?} select the members of the selected groups and layers (or `ids`), as double-clicking the Appearance panel's Contents row does: the panel then lists, and appearance edits change, their own appearance; errors when none has members → {ids}
cmd:appearance.targetContents.desc: Select the members of the selected groups and layers so appearance edits change their own look.

cmd:appearance.transfer.label: Move Appearance
cmd:appearance.transfer.params: {source: id, target: id, copy?: bool} give `target` (a layer, group or object) the appearance (fills, strokes, effects) and transparency (opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout) of `source`, as dragging a target circle onto another in the Layers panel does; the source is left with a cleared appearance (as appearance.clear) unless `copy` (Alt-drag). cmd:artboard.convertToArtboards.label: Convert to Artboards
cmd:artboard.convertToArtboards.params: {} turn each selected object's bounds into a new artboard (the objects are removed) → {artboards}

cmd:artboard.delete.label: Delete Artboard
cmd:artboard.delete.desc: Delete an artboard from the document.

cmd:artboard.duplicate.label: Duplicate Artboard
cmd:artboard.duplicate.params: {index?: n (default: the Artboard tool's artboard), art?: bool (default: the Artboard tool's moveArt option)} copy placed right of the last artboard, with copies of the art fully inside it when `art` (locked and hidden art only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard) → {index, ids: the art's copies}

cmd:artboard.fitToArt.label: Fit to Artwork Bounds
cmd:artboard.fitToArt.desc: Fit an artboard to the bounds of all artwork on it.

cmd:artboard.fitToSelection.label: Fit to Selected Art
cmd:artboard.fitToSelection.desc: Fit an artboard to the bounds of the selected art.

cmd:artboard.move.label: Move Artboard
cmd:artboard.move.params: {index, dx, dy, moveArt?: bool, copy?: bool} move an artboard (and the art fully inside it; locked and hidden art only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard); `copy` (Alt-drag) leaves them and moves copies → {index, moved: the art moved or the copies}

cmd:artboard.new.label: New Artboard
cmd:artboard.new.params: {x?, y?, width?, height?, name?} (default: right of the last)
cmd:artboard.new.desc: Add a new artboard at a given position and size.

cmd:artboard.rearrange.label: Rearrange All Artboards…
cmd:artboard.rearrange.params: {columns?: n (2), spacing?: pt (20), byColumn?: false, moveArtwork?: true (locked and hidden art only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard)} lay artboards out in a grid
cmd:artboard.rearrange.desc: Lay all artboards out in a neat grid with even spacing.

cmd:artboard.reorder.label: Move Artboard Up/Down
cmd:artboard.reorder.desc: Change an artboard's number, moving it up or down in the order.

cmd:artboard.setProps.label: Artboard Options…
cmd:artboard.setProps.desc: Rename an artboard or change its position and size.

cmd:attributes.info.label: Attributes
cmd:attributes.info.params: {ids?, item?} → {ids, overprintFill, overprintStroke, showCenter, imageMap: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url, note, fillRule: "nonZero"|"evenOdd" (of the paths and compound paths in them), reversed (their subpaths run counter-clockwise on screen: Reverse Path Direction On), recentUrls: [newest first]} the Attributes panel's values for `ids` or the selection, overprint aimed as object.setOverprint aims; a value is null where they differ (or nothing has a fill, stroke or path)

cmd:attributes.openUrl.label: Browser

cmd:attributes.set.label: Attributes
cmd:attributes.set.params: {overprintFill?: bool, overprintStroke?: bool (aimed as object.setOverprint's fill and stroke, item? too), showCenter?: bool (the canvas shows the selected object's centre point), imageMap?: "none"|"rectangle"|"polygon", url?: string ("" removes it; SVG export links the object), note?: string, ids?} set the Attributes panel's values on ids or the selection, as one undo step; a URL given joins the recent URLs (attributes.info) → {changed: objects}

cmd:brush.apply.label: Apply Brush

cmd:brush.apply.desc: Apply a brush to the strokes of the selected paths and make it current.

cmd:brush.delete.label: Delete Brush

cmd:brush.delete.desc: Delete a brush; strokes using it become plain strokes.

cmd:brush.duplicate.label: Duplicate Brush
cmd:brush.duplicate.desc: Duplicate a brush under a new name.

cmd:brush.freehand.label: Paintbrush

cmd:brush.freehand.desc: Paint a freehand stroke with a brush.

cmd:brush.get.label: Brush Definition
cmd:brush.get.desc: Get the definition of a brush as json.

cmd:brush.list.label: Brushes
cmd:brush.list.desc: List all brushes and which one is current.

cmd:brush.new.label: New Brush…
cmd:brush.new.params: {type: calligraphic|scatter|art|pattern|bristle, name?, params?: {…definition fields}, ids?} new brush; art/scatter/pattern brushes take the selected art (pattern: side tile) unless params give it → {name}

cmd:brush.options.label: Brush Options…
cmd:brush.options.params: {name, params?: {…fields to change}, newName?} edit a brush definition (strokes using it update) → {name}
cmd:brush.options.desc: Edit a brush definition so strokes using it update.

cmd:brush.remove.label: Remove Brush Stroke
cmd:brush.remove.params: {ids?} remove brushes from the selected strokes → {ids}
cmd:brush.remove.desc: Remove brushes from the selected strokes, leaving plain strokes.

cmd:brush.setCurrent.label: Current Brush
cmd:brush.setCurrent.params: {name: string|null} the brush the Paintbrush tool paints with (not an undo step)
cmd:brush.setCurrent.desc: Choose the brush the paintbrush tool paints with.

cmd:charStyle.apply.label: Apply Character Style
cmd:charStyle.apply.params: {name, clearOverrides?, ids?|id + start?/end? (a Type tool range)} → {count}
cmd:charStyle.apply.desc: Apply a character style to text, optionally clearing manual overrides.

cmd:charStyle.delete.label: Delete Character Style
cmd:charStyle.delete.desc: Delete a character style; the text keeps its look.

cmd:charStyle.duplicate.label: Duplicate Character Style
cmd:charStyle.duplicate.desc: Duplicate a character style under a new name.

cmd:charStyle.list.label: Character Styles
cmd:charStyle.list.desc: List all character styles with their attributes and use counts.

cmd:charStyle.new.label: New Character Style
cmd:charStyle.new.desc: Create a character style, by default from the selected text's formatting.

cmd:charStyle.redefine.label: Redefine Character Style
cmd:charStyle.redefine.params: {name, id?, start?} from the selected text; users keep their overrides
cmd:charStyle.redefine.desc: Redefine a character style from the selected text's formatting.

cmd:charStyle.setAttrs.label: Character Style Options
cmd:charStyle.setAttrs.params: {name, attrs: {…}} replace the style's attributes; users keep their overrides
cmd:charStyle.setAttrs.desc: Replace a character style's attributes; text using the style keeps manual overrides.

cmd:clipboard.exportSvg.label: Clipboard as SVG
cmd:clipboard.exportSvg.params: {} → {svg} the copied objects as standalone SVG (null when the clipboard is empty)
cmd:clipboard.exportSvg.desc: Get the copied objects as standalone svg text from the clipboard.

cmd:clipboard.importSvg.params: {svg | dataBase64 (SVG or SVGZ bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the SVG's objects (and the images, patterns and symbols they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.pasteInPlace

cmd:color.gamutCheck.params: {ids?, colors?: [color]} colours that can't be printed in the working CMYK (selection, or the whole document when nothing is selected) → {checked, outOfGamut: [{hex, deltaE, count}]}

cmd:color.loadProfile.label: Load Color Profile…
cmd:color.loadProfile.params: {path: .icc/.icm file} register an ICC profile (native only) → {name, kind}
cmd:color.loadProfile.desc: Register an icc colour profile from a file.

cmd:color.plates.label: Plates
cmd:color.plates.desc: Report the separation plates with their spot state and visibility.

cmd:colorTheme.addToSwatches.label: Add to Swatches
cmd:colorTheme.addToSwatches.params: {name} add a saved theme's colours to the Swatches panel as a colour group named after it (as swatch.newGroup), as one undo step → {name: the group's, swatches: [names]}
cmd:colorTheme.addToSwatches.desc: Add a saved colour theme's colours to the swatches panel as a colour group.

cmd:colorTheme.list.label: Color Themes
cmd:colorTheme.list.params: {} the saved colour themes, in order → {themes: [{name, colors: ["#rrggbb"], keys: [colour keys, exact in each colour's model], rule?}]}
cmd:colorTheme.list.desc: List the saved colour themes with their colours.

cmd:colorTheme.save.params: {colors: [1–5 colours] | color + rule (a harmony rule id or label, see color.harmony: its 5-colour theme from that base colour, base first), rule?: the rule it was made with, name?: (default "Theme N"), replace?: a saved theme's name (overwrite that theme in place, e.g. after editing it; it may be renamed)} save a colour theme to the local theme library (the preferences) → {name, count: themes saved}
cmd:colorTheme.save.desc: Save colours, or a harmony from a base colour, as a named colour theme.

Each page: TrimBox = artboard, BleedBox = artboard + bleed, MediaBox = that + the marks' room (art clipped to the BleedBox), output?: {conversion: none (default)|destination (every colour into the destination profile's model, CMYK or RGB, also colours of that model in another profile)|preserveNumbers (only colours of the other model and Lab; those in the destination's model keep their numbers) (grey stays grey; images are converted too, printer's marks are not), destination: profile name (edit.colorSettings lists them; default: the document's profile for its colour mode), profiles: none (device colours)|all|destination|taggedSource (documents assigned a profile: edit.assignProfile) (ICC-based colours: CMYK with the destination or document CMYK profile, RGB as sRGB, grey with the sRGB tone curve; PDF/A always), outputIntent: profile name (embedded as the catalog's /GTS_PDFX output intent; a name that isn't a profile is only named, which pdfX1a and pdfX3 allow only with a registry and pdfX4 refuses; pdfX1a needs a CMYK one), outputCondition, outputConditionId (default: outputIntent), registry, trapped (/Trapped /True; /False when an output intent is written)} (PDF/A files keep their own output intent), advanced?: {fontSubsetPercent: 100 (below 100 is accepted with a warning: fonts are always embedded as subsets), outlineText: true (false: type as real, selectable and searchable text in embedded subset fonts with a ToUnicode map; fonts whose licence forbids embedding, or allows only whole fonts, stay outlines with a warning), overprint: preserve (overprinting fills and strokes set /OP /op true, /OPM 1; white ones knock out with document.setup discardWhiteOverprint)|discard (they knock out)}, security?: {openPassword, permissionsPassword, printing: none|low|high, changes: none|pages|forms|comments|any, copy, screenReader, plaintextMetadata}} → {path, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, bytes, warnings}. The options apply over the preset (null keeps its value); options accepted but not applied yet come back as warnings; a standard with a PDF version it doesn't allow and a password with a standard are refused, and so is a PDF/X file that would still break its standard (transparency the flattener left, RGB in pdfX1a, a font not embedded) or a PDF 1.3 file with transparency left. document.export {format: pdf} takes the same options
cmd:document.exportPdf.desc: Export the document as a PDF with preset, pages and standards options.

cmd:document.info.desc: Report document statistics: objects, colours, fonts, images and more.

cmd:document.inspect.params: {depth?, childLimit?} → layer tree, artboards, selection, history (a sliced tree reports childCount)
cmd:document.inspect.desc: Return the layer tree, artboards, selection and history for inspection.

cmd:document.json.label: Document JSON
cmd:document.json.desc: Get the complete document model as json.

cmd:document.node.desc: Return one object's full details and children for inspection.

cmd:document.open.label: Open Document
cmd:document.open.params: {path} or {name, dataBase64}, PDF/.ai: pages?: "2-3, 5" (1-based, default all; one artboard each) | page?: n, cropTo?: bounding|art|crop (default)|trim|bleed|media (the box each artboard gets; bounding: the art's bounds), password? (encrypted PDFs; see document.pdfInfo), textAs?: text (default: point type per line, in the file's fonts by name; missing ones are listed in warnings) | outlines (glyph paths), layers?: true (default: optional content groups become layers with their visibility, print state and lock — art that is off comes in as a hidden layer; other art goes to a layer per page) | false (one layer per page, without the art that is off; Save then asks for a name), colorMode?: rgb|cmyk (the mode the document opens in, its colours converted as file.documentColorMode does, grays? as there; default: the file's — a PDF keeps CMYK, Gray and spot inks (spot swatches at a tint) and opens in CMYK when painted mostly in CMYK), DXF: dxf?: {layout?: "Model" (default) | a paper layout's name (document.dxfInfo lists them), unit?, scale? (the ratio: 1 unit of the art = scale drawing units; default: the drawing at 1:1 in its own unit), fit?: false (scale to fit an artboard of fitTo?: [612, 792], turned to the art's orientation), scaleLineweights?: false (lineweights scale with the art), center?: true (false: the drawing's origin on the artboard's bottom-left corner; fitted art's bottom-left corner), mergeLayers?: false (all art on one layer)} → {index, title, format, warnings, restored, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks: [{name, path, ids}]}; any readable format (see document.formats): .vectorcraft/.drawcraft, .svg/.svgz, .pdf/.ai, .ait, ASCII .dxf (each DXF layer with art a layer; blocks symbols; what can't come in is listed in warnings), PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP/TIFF/BMP (an image opens as a document of its pixel size), .emf/.wmf (one artboard, the picture's frame; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning), .eps and PostScript .ai (one artboard, the bounding box: an EPS file VectorCraft wrote restores the document it carries, restored: true; other files are read by a PostScript interpreter — paths, colours and spot inks, clips, gradients, images, type in the fonts named — and come in as their TIFF preview, with a warning, when their PostScript can't be read). A PDF/.ai/.ait or SVG saved with Preserve Editing restores the native document it carries (restored: true; a PDF only when no pages are picked), unless the file was changed elsewhere since or the data can't be read: then its artwork is imported and the first warning says why. Templates (native templates, .ait) open as a new untitled document; a restored .ai keeps its path (Save writes .ai again). Linked images are read from their files (looked for at their path, then relative to the document): missing ones show their saved preview (links.relink), modified ones are read again only with Preferences › Update Links: Automatically (else links.update). An SVG's <image> files (relative links from the SVG's folder) stay linked, SVG files become art, missing ones a placeholder in their box (a warning and missingLinks)
cmd:document.open.desc: Open a file as a document, with PDF page and password options.

cmd:document.pdfSettings.label: PDF Settings
cmd:document.pdfSettings.params: {preset?, includeDocument?: false, …document.exportPdf options} → {settings (the preset with the options applied), presets: [name…], changed: [{option: "compression.compressText", value}] (what differs from the preset), warnings}; includeDocument also exports the active document in memory and adds its warnings (knockout groups approximated, effects left out…)
cmd:document.pdfSettings.desc: Resolve a PDF preset with options and report what changed.

cmd:document.rasterEffectsSettings.label: Document Raster Effects Settings…
cmd:document.rasterEffectsSettings.params: {resolution?: ppi (1–2400) | "screen" (72) | "medium" (150) | "high" (300), colorModel?: "rgb"|"cmyk" (the document's mode)|"grayscale"|"bitmap", background?: "transparent"|"white", antiAlias?: bool (off: hard edges), clippingMask?: bool (white background only under the art; Rasterize clips to the art), addAround?: pt (0–1000, room around the art), preserveSpotColors?: bool (stored)} how raster effects (shadows, glows, blurs, feathers) become images in PDF export and Expand Appearance, and the defaults of object.rasterize; one undo step; always → the settings
cmd:document.rasterEffectsSettings.desc: Set the resolution and colour model used when rasterizing effects.

cmd:document.save.label: Save Document
cmd:document.save.params: {path?, format?: vectorcraft|template|pdf|svg|svgz|ai (default: the path's extension, else the document's own format), options?: {…the format's options, see file.formatOptions; default: as last saved}, svg?: {…SVG options} (SVG options may also be given flat; an SVG save keeps hidden layers, display:none, unless hiddenLayers is false), native (also flat): compress?: bool (gzip; default: the useCompression preference), version?: 3 (2 or 1: for older VectorCraft versions, never compressed), preview?: false (embed a PNG of the first artboard, at most 256 px), native and .ai: separateArtboards?: false (also save each artboard of range?: "1-3, 5"|"all" (default) to <name>-<artboard>.<ext> beside the file, holding that artboard and the art touching it; the result's files lists every file written), includeLinked?: false (keep linked files' own pixels, not just their previews; they stay linked), embedProfiles?: true (carry the ICC profiles loaded from files that the document is tagged with; opening the file installs them where missing), pdfCompatible?: false for native (also carry a PDF of every artboard) | true for .ai (false: blank pages, only the native document), .ai: compress?: true (compression.compressText), modified?: Unix seconds|null (the File Info modified date, and created date when there is none, a save to a file stamps; default now, recorded in the journal so a replay matches; null: leave the dates)} → {path, format, bytes, warnings, files?: [path…] (the file and its artboards' files), linked?: [path…] (images an SVG links to)}. Save writes one artboard, except a .ai file: a PDF-compatible file of every artboard carrying the native document (preserveEditing always on; PDF options flat or in options), which document.open restores exactly; separateArtboards writes more files, one per artboard. Without a path it writes the document's own file in its own format: a document opened from or saved as SVG/PDF saves as that again (warnings name what the format loses). No path known (never saved, converted from an older version, restored by Data Recovery, or another format) → {dataBase64, format, name, folder?, warnings} and the document stays modified
cmd:document.save.desc: Save the document to a file in its own or another format.

cmd:document.serialize.label: Serialize Document
cmd:document.serialize.params: {format?: vectorcraft (default)|template|svg|svgz|pdf|png|jpg|webp|gif|png8|txt|dxf|eps|emf|wmf|tiff|bmp|tga|psd, …the format's options (see document.formats; SVG ones also as svg: {…}), selectedOnly?: false (the selected objects alone, in their layers)} → {text, warnings} for svg (plus dataBase64, the file, when its encoding isn't UTF-8), else {dataBase64, warnings}; an SVG of several artboards also gives files: [{name, text}], linked images linked: [{name, dataBase64}]
cmd:document.serialize.desc: Return the document as text or data in a chosen format without saving a file.

cmd:document.setUnits.label: Units
cmd:document.setUnits.params: {units: "Points"|"Picas"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|"Centimeters"|"Pixels"|"Feet & Inches"|"Meters"|"Yards"|"Feet"} the document's units: every length the UI shows and reads (General)
cmd:document.setUnits.desc: Set the document's measurement units for everything the interface shows.

cmd:edit.assignProfile.label: Assign Profile…
cmd:edit.assignProfile.params: {rgb?: profile|null, cmyk?: profile|null} tag the document with profiles (colour numbers are kept) → {rgb, cmyk}
cmd:edit.assignProfile.desc: Tag the document with rgb or cmyk colour profiles without converting colour numbers.

cmd:edit.clear.label: Clear
cmd:edit.clear.params: {ids?} delete the objects `ids`, else the selection (direct-selected anchors, else objects, else ruler guides)
cmd:edit.clear.desc: Delete the selection, direct-selected anchors, or ruler guides.

cmd:edit.colorSettings.label: Color Settings…
cmd:edit.colorSettings.params: {rgb?: profile, cmyk?: profile, intent?: "perceptual"|"relative"|"saturation"|"absolute", bpc?: bool} set the working spaces → {rgb, cmyk, intent, bpc, profiles: [{name, kind, builtin}]}
cmd:edit.colorSettings.desc: Set the working colour spaces and rendering intent for colour conversions.

cmd:edit.colors.blendHorizontally.desc: Grade the fills of objects between the leftmost and rightmost colours.

cmd:edit.colors.blendVertically.desc: Grade the fills of objects between the topmost and bottommost colours.

cmd:edit.colors.invert.params: {fill?: true, stroke?: true, includeImages?: true, includePatterns?: true, ids?} replace each colour by its RGB inverse (keeps the colour model) in fills, strokes, text, gradient meshes (with fills), embedded images (a recoloured copy) and pattern tiles (a new pattern swatch; the original stays), as one undo step → {changed}
cmd:edit.colors.invert.desc: Replace colours by their inverses in fills, strokes, text, meshes, images and patterns.

cmd:edit.colors.overprintBlack.label: Overprint Black…
cmd:edit.colors.overprintBlack.params: {remove?: false, percentage?: 100, fill?: true, stroke?: true, includeCmyBlacks?: false, includeSpotBlacks?: false, ids?} make the black fills and/or strokes of the selection (or ids; groups: their contents; type: its characters) overprint, or stop (remove). cmd:edit.colors.overprintBlack.desc: Make the black fills or strokes of the selection overprint, or stop overprinting.

cmd:edit.colors.saturate.desc: Scale the saturation of the selection's colours up or down.

cmd:edit.colors.toGrayscale.desc: Convert the colours of the selection to grayscale.

cmd:edit.colors.toRGB.desc: Convert the colours of the selection to rgb.

cmd:edit.cut.desc: Cut the selection to the clipboard, removing it.

cmd:edit.duplicate.desc: Duplicate the selection in place, optionally offset.

cmd:edit.findNext.desc: Select the next text object containing the searched text.

cmd:edit.findReplace.desc: Find and replace text across every text object.

cmd:edit.pasteInFront.desc: Paste in place just above the top selected object.

cmd:edit.pasteInPlace.desc: Paste objects exactly where they were copied from.

cmd:edit.pasteOnAllArtboards.label: Paste on All Artboards

cmd:edit.pasteOnAllArtboards.desc: Paste a copy on every artboard at the same relative offset.

cmd:edit.pasteWithoutFormatting.label: Paste without Formatting
cmd:edit.pasteWithoutFormatting.params: {center?, dx?, dy?, swatchConflict?} paste as edit.paste; pasted text takes the default character style (one run) and leaves its character and paragraph styles behind → {ids, added, merged, renamed}
cmd:edit.pasteWithoutFormatting.desc: Paste text stripped to the default character style.

cmd:effect.apply.params: {effect: id (see effect.list, e.g. "stylize.dropShadow", "distort.roughen", "warp.arc", or "plugin.<id>" for an installed effect plug-in), params?: {…} (missing keys take the dialog defaults), item?: appearance item index|null (apply to that fill/stroke only; omitted: the Appearance panel's active item, else the whole object), ids?: [..] (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents" (contents: the objects inside groups and layers)} append a live effect to each selected object's appearance (a group's or layer's apply to its members as one piece: one combined shadow; a Pathfinder effect, which combines a group's contents, groups several loose selected objects first, in the same undo step) → {ids, index, item, grouped?}

cmd:file.documentColorMode.params: {mode: "cmyk"|"rgb", convert?: true (convert every colour of the art, symbols, pattern tiles and swatches through the colour settings; swatch links kept; Gray colours stay Gray, on the black plate), intent?, grays?: "profile" (default: RGB greys separate through the CMYK profile like any colour, into four-colour greys and a rich black) | "black" (to CMYK, RGB greys with R = G = B go on the black plate only, K = their grey value)} → {changed}

cmd:file.export.svg.label: Export As SVG…
cmd:file.export.svg.params: {} opens SVG Options; with params = document.export {path?, svg?: {…SVG options}, range?…} (a .svgz path writes it gzipped)
cmd:file.export.svg.desc: Open svg options, or export the artwork as svg or svgz with given options.

cmd:file.exportForScreens.label: Export for Screens…
cmd:file.exportForScreens.params: {} opens the dialog (on the document's last settings); with params = document.exportForScreens (no folder on the web: downloads the files or the zip; openLocation: shows the first file in the file manager)
cmd:file.exportForScreens.desc: Open the Export for Screens dialog on the document's last settings.

cmd:file.info.label: File Info…
cmd:file.info.params: {title?, author?, authorTitle?, description?, keywords?: [string…]|"a, b" (each once), rating?: 0–5, copyrightStatus?: "unknown"|"copyrighted"|"publicDomain", copyrightNotice?, copyrightUrl?} set the File Info in one undo step (SVG with metadata, PDF and PNG exports carry it); no params → {title, author, authorTitle, description, keywords, rating, copyrightStatus, copyrightNotice, copyrightUrl, created, modified (ISO 8601 UTC or null; read-only), colorMode, units, artboards, objects}
cmd:file.info.desc: Set the document's metadata: title, author, keywords, rating and copyright.

cmd:file.new.label: New…
cmd:file.new.params: {preset?: a name from file.newPresets (start from it; the other params change it), name?|title?: document name (default Untitled-N), width?: pt=612|"210 mm", height?: pt=792, units?: "Pixels"|"Points"|"Picas"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|"Centimeters"|"Feet"|"Yards"|"Meters"|"Feet & Inches" (default: prefs unitsGeneral, as print presets; screen presets: Pixels), orientation?: "portrait"|"landscape" (swaps width and height to match), artboards?: n (1–1000), artboardLayout?: {layout?: "gridByRow"|"gridByColumn"|"row"|"column", columns?: n (default: all in one row), spacing?: pt=20, rightToLeft?: bool}, bleed?: pt|[top, bottom, left, right]|{top?, …} (0–72 pt), backgroundContents?: "transparent"|"white" (a white artboard background, not an object), colorMode?: "rgb"|"cmyk" (a CMYK document starts with CMYK swatches and stores the colours applied to it as CMYK), rasterEffectsPpi?: 72|150|300 (1–2400), previewMode?: "default"|"pixel"|"overprint" (overprint turns Overprint Preview on, pixel Pixel Preview in the app; default leaves both), created?: Unix seconds|null (File Info's created date; default now, recorded in the journal so a replay matches)} → {index, previewMode}; the size is remembered in file.newPresets' Recent
cmd:file.new.desc: Create a new document from a preset or custom size and colour settings.

cmd:file.newFromTemplate.label: New from Template…
cmd:file.newFromTemplate.params: {path} or {name, dataBase64}: open a template (or any readable file) as a new untitled document → {index, title, format, warnings}
cmd:file.newFromTemplate.desc: Open a template file as a new untitled document.

cmd:file.open.label: Open…
cmd:file.open.params: {path?} → with a path, document.open's result {index, title, format, warnings, …} (null when a dialog asks first or a library loads)
cmd:file.open.desc: Open the file picker, or open a file at a given path.

cmd:file.openRecent1.label: Open Recent File 1
cmd:file.openRecent1.desc: Open the most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent10.label: Open Recent File 10
cmd:file.openRecent10.desc: Open the tenth most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent2.label: Open Recent File 2
cmd:file.openRecent2.desc: Open the second most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent3.label: Open Recent File 3
cmd:file.openRecent3.desc: Open the third most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent4.label: Open Recent File 4
cmd:file.openRecent4.desc: Open the fourth most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent5.label: Open Recent File 5
cmd:file.openRecent5.desc: Open the fifth most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent6.label: Open Recent File 6
cmd:file.openRecent6.desc: Open the sixth most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent7.label: Open Recent File 7
cmd:file.openRecent7.desc: Open the seventh most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent8.label: Open Recent File 8
cmd:file.openRecent8.desc: Open the eighth most recently used file.

cmd:file.openRecent9.label: Open Recent File 9
cmd:file.openRecent9.desc: Open the ninth most recently used file.

cmd:file.place.label: Place…
cmd:file.place.params: {path? | paths?} no file: pick files, then the Place dialog (Link, Template, Replace); paths: that dialog for them; path (or name+dataBase64, …file.place params): file.place, centred in the view (a PDF with several pages or a password and no page opens the Place PDF dialog first)
cmd:file.place.desc: Place image or drawing files into the document, linked or embedded.

cmd:file.recentFiles.label: Recent Files
cmd:file.recentFiles.desc: List the recent files, newest first.

cmd:file.revert.label: Revert
cmd:file.revert.params: {} discard the changes: reload the saved file into the same tab (history cleared; the tab keeps its place and view). Saved, modified documents only; if the file can't be read the document is left as it is → {path}. The app asks first (a confirm dialog) unless confirmed: true
cmd:file.revert.desc: Reload the saved file, discarding all changes since the last save.

cmd:file.save.label: Save
cmd:file.save.params: {path?, format?, options?, svg?: {…SVG options}} = document.save, written through the app (a document saved as SVG, PDF or .ai, or opened from one Save can write back, saves as that again, with the same options); with no path known (never saved, converted) the Save As panel asks first
cmd:file.save.desc: Save the document through the app, asking where when never saved.

cmd:file.saveAs.label: Save As…
cmd:file.saveAs.params: {path?, format?: vectorcraft|template|pdf|svg|svgz|ai (default: the path's extension, else the document's own), options?, svg?, modified? (as document.save)} the document takes on the new path, name and format (except a template, which is always a copy) → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name, folder?, warnings}
cmd:file.saveAs.desc: Save the document under a new path, name or format.

cmd:file.saveAsTemplate.label: Save as Template…
cmd:file.saveAsTemplate.params: {path?, compress?, version?, preview? (as document.save)} a native template (.vctemplate) that opens as a new untitled document; the document is unchanged → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name: "<name> template.vctemplate", folder: the Templates folder (preference templatesFolder), warnings}
cmd:file.saveAsTemplate.desc: Save the document as a reusable template that opens untitled.

cmd:file.saveCopy.label: Save a Copy…
cmd:file.saveCopy.params: {path?, format?, options?} (as file.saveAs) write a copy; the document keeps its path, title and modified state → {path, format, bytes, warnings}; no path → {dataBase64, format, name: "<name> copy.<ext>", folder?, warnings}
cmd:file.saveCopy.desc: Write a copy of the document while keeping working on the original.

cmd:flattener.presets.delete.label: Delete Transparency Flattener Preset
cmd:flattener.presets.delete.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}
cmd:flattener.presets.delete.desc: Delete a saved transparency flattener preset, keeping the built-in ones.

cmd:flattener.presets.export.label: Export Transparency Flattener Presets
cmd:flattener.presets.export.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcflattener file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}
cmd:flattener.presets.export.desc: Write transparency flattener presets to a flattener presets file.

cmd:flattener.presets.import.label: Import Transparency Flattener Presets
cmd:flattener.presets.import.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else the imported ones get a number)} add the presets of a .vcflattener file (as flattener.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}
cmd:flattener.presets.import.desc: Import transparency flattener presets from a flattener presets file.

cmd:flattener.presets.list.label: Transparency Flattener Presets
cmd:flattener.presets.list.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, options}]} the built-in presets (High, Medium and Low Resolution), then the saved ones; any of these names works as `preset` wherever flattener options are taken
cmd:flattener.presets.list.desc: List the built-in and saved transparency flattener presets.

cmd:flattener.presets.save.label: Save Transparency Flattener Preset
cmd:flattener.presets.save.params: {name?: (default: a new "Flattener Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else medium), …options (the keys of object.flattenTransparency, at the top level or in `options`)} create or change a saved preset (built-in ones can't change) → {name, options, created}
cmd:flattener.presets.save.desc: Create or update a saved transparency flattener preset from flattener options.

cmd:flattener.preview.label: Flattener Preview
cmd:flattener.preview.params: {highlight?: "none"|"rasterizedRegions" (areas the raster/vector balance rasterizes whole)|"transparentObjects"|"allAffected"|"expandedPatterns" (pattern art taking part)|"outlinedStrokes"|"outlinedText"|"allRasterized" (default none), overprints?: "preserve"|"simulate"|"discard" (simulate and discard flatten without preserveOverprints), preset?, …options (as object.flattenTransparency), ids?: (default: the whole document)} what flattening would do, without changing anything → {highlight, regions: [{bounds: {x, y, width, height}, id?}] (the highlighted objects, or areas), counts: {transparentObjects, allAffected, expandedPatterns, outlinedStrokes, outlinedText, rasterizedRegions, allRasterized, vectorRegions}, options}
cmd:flattener.preview.desc: Highlight which areas flattening will rasterize, outline or affect in the artwork.

cmd:gradient.selectStop.label: Select Gradient Stop
cmd:gradient.selectStop.params: {index: stop index (0 = the start) | null to clear} select a stop of the gradient behind the active proxy (the first selected object's, else the default paint): the stop the Gradient tool's annotator, the Gradient and Color panels and Delete/arrow keys act on → {index}
cmd:gradient.selectStop.desc: Select a gradient stop so panels and tools act on it.

cmd:graph.create.label: Create Graph
cmd:graph.create.params: {type: column|stackedColumn|bar|stackedBar|line|area|scatter|pie|radar, x, y, width, height, series?: [..], categories?: [..], rows?: [[..]], csv?} → {id}
cmd:graph.create.desc: Create a column, bar, line, pie, radar or other graph from data.

cmd:graph.setData.label: Data…
cmd:graph.setData.params: {id?, series?, categories?, rows?, csv?: first row = series labels (first cell empty), then one row per category: label, values…} replace the graph's data; no data → the current {csv, series, categories, rows}
cmd:graph.setData.desc: Replace a graph's data, series and categories, or read the current data.

cmd:graph.setType.label: Type…
cmd:graph.setType.params: {id?, type?, columnWidth?: %, clusterWidth?: %, legend?: bool, markPoints?: bool, connectPoints?: bool, ticks?: n, axisMin?, axisMax?} change the graph type and options; no options → the current ones
cmd:graph.setType.desc: Change a graph's type and options such as column width, legend and axis.

cmd:graphicStyle.addFromLibrary.label: Add to Graphic Styles
cmd:graphicStyle.addFromLibrary.params: {library: id or name, name? | names?: [style names in the library] (default: all of it), apply?: false (also apply the first one to `ids` or the selection, if any, as graphicStyle.apply), add?: false (with apply: add its appearance on top, as Alt-click), ids?} copy library styles into the document's Graphic Styles as one undo step (with the apply). A style the document already has (same name and look) isn't added again; a name taken by another style gets a number ("Halo 2"). The patterns they paint with come along (a name taken by another pattern or swatch gets a number) → {library, added: [names in the document], existing: [names already there], applied?: name}
cmd:graphicStyle.addFromLibrary.desc: Copy styles from a graphic style library into the document's graphic styles panel.

cmd:graphicStyle.apply.label: Apply Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.apply.params: {name, add?: bool, ids? (layers too), target?: "object"|"contents"} give the objects (default: the selection; a group or layer itself, its fills and strokes painting its members and its effects applying to them as one piece; target contents: the objects inside instead) the style's appearance, opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout, and link them to it (placed gradients land at the same place relative to each object's bounds); add: true (Alt-click) adds its fills, strokes and effects on top of the existing appearance instead and unlinks. With nothing selected (and no ids) the next object drawn takes the style instead (see appearance.newArt) → {newArt: true}
cmd:graphicStyle.apply.desc: Apply a graphic style to objects, optionally stacking it on top.

cmd:graphicStyle.breakLink.label: Break Link to Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.breakLink.params: {ids?} unlink the objects (default: the selection) from their graphic style; they keep their look
cmd:graphicStyle.breakLink.desc: Unlink objects from their graphic style while keeping their look.

cmd:graphicStyle.delete.label: Delete Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.delete.params: {name} | {names: [name…]} delete styles; their objects keep their look but are unlinked
cmd:graphicStyle.delete.desc: Delete graphic styles; their objects keep their look but are unlinked.

cmd:graphicStyle.duplicate.label: Duplicate Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.duplicate.desc: Duplicate a graphic style under a new name.

cmd:graphicStyle.libraries.label: Graphic Style Libraries
cmd:graphicStyle.libraries.params: {} → {libraries: [{id, name, category: "builtIn"|"user" (User Defined: the .vcstyles files in the user library folder, rescanned now)|"loaded" (graphicStyle.loadLibrary), count, path?}], userFolder} every graphic style library the library panel opens, in menu order
cmd:graphicStyle.libraries.desc: List every graphic style library the library panel can open.

cmd:graphicStyle.library.label: Graphic Style Library
cmd:graphicStyle.library.params: {library: id or name} → {id, name, category, styles: [{name, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fills, strokes, effects: [effect id…], opacity, blend, isolate, knockout}] (as graphicStyle.list)}
cmd:graphicStyle.library.desc: Read the styles held in one graphic style library.

cmd:graphicStyle.list.label: List Graphic Styles
cmd:graphicStyle.list.params: {} → {styles: [{id, name, fill, stroke, strokeWidth, fills, strokes, effects: [effect id…], opacity: 0..100, blend, isolate, knockout: "on"|"off"|"neutral", linked: [object ids]}], selected: the style the first selected object is linked to, or null, overrideCharColor}
cmd:graphicStyle.list.desc: List the document's graphic styles with their fills, strokes, effects and transparency.

cmd:graphicStyle.loadLibrary.label: Other Library…
cmd:graphicStyle.loadLibrary.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, name?: file name (default: the path's)} load a .vcstyles library, or the graphic styles of any document VectorCraft opens (see document.formats), for the library panel (Window → Graphic Style Libraries lists it until the app quits) → {library: id, name, count}
cmd:graphicStyle.loadLibrary.desc: Load a styles library file, or another document's graphic styles, into the library panel.

cmd:graphicStyle.merge.label: Merge Graphic Styles
cmd:graphicStyle.merge.params: {names: [name…] (two or more), name?} add a style combining the styles' fills, strokes and effects (each style's on top of the ones before it) with the first one's opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout → {name}
cmd:graphicStyle.merge.desc: Merge two or more graphic styles into one combined style.

cmd:graphicStyle.move.label: Move Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.move.params: {name, to: index} move the style to position `to` of the list (0 = first, clamped), as dragging it in the Graphic Styles panel does
cmd:graphicStyle.move.desc: Move a graphic style to another position in the panel.

cmd:graphicStyle.new.label: New Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.new.params: {name?, id?} a style from object `id` or the first selected object: its appearance, opacity, blend mode, isolate and knockout (a group without fills or strokes of its own lends its topmost object's, type its characters'; placed gradients are kept relative to its bounds); links the object. Names are made unique → {name}
cmd:graphicStyle.new.desc: Create a graphic style from an object's or the selection's appearance.

cmd:graphicStyle.redefine.label: Redefine Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.redefine.params: {name?, id?} replace the style (default: the one the object was last linked to) with the look of object `id` or the first selected object; the objects still linked to it update, and that object becomes linked → {name}
cmd:graphicStyle.redefine.desc: Replace a graphic style's look with an object's; linked objects update.

cmd:graphicStyle.rename.label: Rename Graphic Style
cmd:graphicStyle.rename.params: {name, to} (Graphic Style Options; names are unique and linked objects stay linked) → {name}
cmd:graphicStyle.rename.desc: Rename a graphic style, keeping linked objects linked.

cmd:graphicStyle.saveLibrary.label: Save Graphic Style Library…
cmd:graphicStyle.saveLibrary.params: {path?, names?: [style names] (default: all), name?: library name (default: the document's), user?: false (save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined)} save the document's graphic styles as a .vcstyles library (JSON: the styles, unlinked from swatches, and the patterns they paint with) → {path, count, library?: id when saved to the user folder}; without path or user → {data: the file's text, count}
cmd:graphicStyle.saveLibrary.desc: Save graphic styles as a styles library file.

cmd:graphicStyle.setOptions.label: Graphic Styles Options
cmd:graphicStyle.setOptions.params: {overrideCharColor?: bool} Override Character Color (the preference `overrideCharColor`, on by default): applying a style to type replaces its characters' fill and stroke with the style's fills and strokes → {overrideCharColor}
cmd:graphicStyle.setOptions.desc: Set the override character color option for graphic styles applied to text.

cmd:graphicStyle.sortByName.label: Sort by Name
cmd:graphicStyle.sortByName.params: {} sort the styles by name (the Default Graphic Style stays first)
cmd:graphicStyle.sortByName.desc: Sort the graphic styles by name.

cmd:graphicStyle.unused.label: Select All Unused
cmd:graphicStyle.unused.params: {} → {names: [the styles no object is linked to]} (the panel selects them)
cmd:graphicStyle.unused.desc: Find the graphic styles no object is linked to.

cmd:guide.add.label: Add Guide
cmd:guide.add.params: {vertical: bool, pos: pt (x for vertical, y for horizontal), artboard?: index (an artboard guide: it runs across that artboard only and moves, is copied and is deleted with it; default a canvas guide, across the whole canvas)} → {index}
cmd:guide.add.desc: Add a vertical or horizontal ruler guide, canvas-wide or per artboard.

cmd:guide.move.label: Move Guide
cmd:guide.move.params: {index, pos: pt} put ruler guide `index` at `pos` | {dx?, dy?: pt, copy?: bool} move the selected guides (vertical ones by dx, horizontal ones by dy); copy leaves them and selects the moved copies
cmd:guide.move.desc: Move a ruler guide to a position or nudge the selected guides.

cmd:guide.remove.label: Remove Guide
cmd:guide.remove.params: {index?} delete ruler guide `index`, else the selected ones (as Delete / edit.clear does) → {count}
cmd:guide.remove.desc: Delete a ruler guide or all selected guides.

cmd:help.appPage.label: VectorCraft on getartcraft.com
cmd:help.appPage.desc: Open this app's page on the vendor website.

cmd:help.commandPalette.label: Search Commands…
cmd:help.commandPalette.desc: Open the command palette to search commands.

cmd:help.github.label: VectorCraft on GitHub
cmd:help.github.desc: Open the vectorcraft github repository for source, issues and releases.

cmd:help.links.label: Links
cmd:help.links.desc: Shows helpful links to the application's website, app page, and GitHub repository so you can find more information and support.

cmd:imageTrace.expand.label: Expand
cmd:imageTrace.expand.params: {id?} keep only the traced paths (drop the source image) → {ids}
cmd:imageTrace.expand.desc: Keep only the traced paths of an image trace, dropping the source image.

cmd:imageTrace.make.label: Make
cmd:imageTrace.make.params: {id?: image or Image Trace group (default: selection), preset?: name (imageTrace.presets), params?: {mode: "blackAndWhite"|"grayscale"|"color", threshold: 0-255, colors: 2-256, paths: 0-100, corners: 0-100, noise: px, method: "abutting"|"overlapping", ignoreWhite, snapCurvesToLines}} → {id, paths, anchors, colors}
cmd:imageTrace.make.desc: Trace a raster image into vector paths with mode, threshold, colour and noise settings.

cmd:imageTrace.makeAndExpand.label: Make and Expand
cmd:imageTrace.makeAndExpand.params: same as imageTrace.make, then expand → {id, paths, anchors, colors}
cmd:imageTrace.makeAndExpand.desc: Trace an image into vector paths and immediately expand them into editable art.

cmd:imageTrace.presets.label: Image Trace Presets
cmd:imageTrace.presets.desc: List the image trace presets with their parameters.

cmd:imageTrace.release.label: Release
cmd:imageTrace.release.params: {id?} put the source image back in place of Image Trace groups → {ids}
cmd:imageTrace.release.desc: Put the original image back in place of an image trace.

cmd:layer.clippingMask.toggle.label: Make/Release Clipping Mask
cmd:layer.clippingMask.toggle.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the one highlighted layer or group row, else the one selected group, else the current layer)} make: its top object (a path, compound path or text, which loses its paint) clips the rest and moves to the bottom (new art added on top is clipped); release: it stops clipping, the clipping path stays unpainted → {clip}
cmd:layer.clippingMask.toggle.desc: Make or release a clipping mask on a layer or group.

cmd:layer.collectInNew.label: Collect in New Layer
cmd:layer.collectInNew.params: {ids?} move rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was (a sublayer when they are in a layer) → {id}
cmd:layer.collectInNew.desc: Move selected rows or objects into a brand-new layer.

cmd:layer.delete.label: Delete Selection
cmd:layer.delete.params: {ids?|id?} delete rows: layers, sublayers, groups or objects with what they hold (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer). The last layer stays → {deleted}
cmd:layer.delete.desc: Delete highlighted rows or the current layer with everything they hold.

cmd:layer.duplicate.label: Duplicate Selection
cmd:layer.duplicate.params: {ids?|id?} copy rows (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), each just above its original; a layer's copy is named `<name> copy`. The copies are highlighted → {ids}
cmd:layer.duplicate.desc: Copy highlighted rows or the current layer just above the originals.

cmd:layer.new.label: New Layer…
cmd:layer.new.params: {name?, top?: bool, color?, template?, locked?, visible?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?} a layer directly above the current layer, at its level (a sublayer beside a current sublayer); `top`: above all layers (Ctrl-click the button). Options as layer.setProps → {id}
cmd:layer.new.desc: Add a new layer with options for name, colour and visibility.

cmd:layer.newSublayer.label: New Sublayer…
cmd:layer.newSublayer.params: {parent?: layer id (default: the highlighted row's layer, else the current layer), name?, options as layer.new} a sublayer on top of the parent's contents → {id}
cmd:layer.newSublayer.desc: Add a sublayer on top of a parent layer's contents.

cmd:layer.selectAll.label: Select Art
cmd:layer.selectAll.params: {id, add?: bool} the Layers panel's selection column: select the visible, unlocked art of a layer (its sublayers' too), or the object itself; `add` (Shift-click) adds it to the selection, or removes it when it is all selected already → {selected: [..]}
cmd:layer.selectAll.desc: Select all visible, unlocked art of a layer, or the object itself.

cmd:layer.setCurrent.label: Set Current Layer
cmd:layer.setCurrent.params: {id} click a row: it alone is highlighted, and the layer it is (or the layer it is in) becomes the current layer, where new art goes. Not an undo step → {id, layer}
cmd:layer.setCurrent.desc: Make a row's layer the current one where new art goes.

cmd:layer.setProps.label: Layer Options…
cmd:layer.setProps.params: {ids?|id? (default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer), name?, visible?, locked?, template?, printable?, preview?, dimImages?: 0..100|false, color?: index 0..26|"#rrggbb"|preset name} Layer Options; rows that are not layers take name, visible and locked. Template on also locks the layer and dims its images to 50% (unless given); off unlocks it and stops dimming. One undo step
cmd:layer.setProps.desc: Change a layer's name, colour, template, lock, print and preview options.

cmd:layer.target.label: Target
cmd:layer.target.params: {id} target a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle in the Layers panel does: a layer gets its visible, unlocked art (its sublayers' too) selected and becomes the current layer, and appearance.*, effect.*, transparency.* and the opacity-mask commands without `ids` then act on the layer itself; anything else is selected. Any other selection change ends the targeting (`document.inspect` → target) → {id, selected: [..]}
cmd:layer.target.desc: Target a layer, group or object as clicking its Layers panel circle does.

cmd:livePaint.expand.label: Expand
cmd:livePaint.expand.params: {id?} turn Live Paint groups into plain groups of their painted faces and edges → {ids}
cmd:livePaint.expand.desc: Turn live paint groups into plain groups of their painted faces and edges.

cmd:livePaint.fill.label: Live Paint Bucket
cmd:livePaint.fill.params: {group?: id | ids?: [id…] (paths to make live first), point: [x,y], color?|swatch?|gradient?|none? (default: current fill)} fill the face containing point → {group, face}
cmd:livePaint.fill.desc: Fill the face under a point of a live paint group with a colour.

cmd:livePaint.info.label: Live Paint Info
cmd:livePaint.info.params: {group} → {faces: [{id, fill, bounds}], edges: [{id, stroke, width}], sources}
cmd:livePaint.info.desc: Report the faces, edges and source paths of a live paint group.

cmd:livePaint.make.label: Make
cmd:livePaint.make.params: {ids?} build a Live Paint group from the selected paths → {id, faces, edges}
cmd:livePaint.make.desc: Build a live paint group from the selected paths.

cmd:livePaint.merge.label: Merge
cmd:livePaint.merge.params: {ids?} add the other selected paths (and Live Paint groups) to the first Live Paint group, keeping its paint → {id, faces, edges}
cmd:livePaint.merge.desc: Add selected paths into an existing live paint group, keeping its paint.

cmd:livePaint.release.label: Release
cmd:livePaint.release.params: {id?} replace Live Paint groups with their original paths → {ids}
cmd:livePaint.release.desc: Release live paint groups back to their original paths.

cmd:livePaint.strokeEdge.label: Live Paint Bucket (Stroke)
cmd:livePaint.strokeEdge.params: {group: id, point: [x,y], color?|swatch?|none? (default: current stroke), width?: pt (default: current weight), tolerance?: pt (4)} paint the edge nearest point → {group, edge}
cmd:livePaint.strokeEdge.desc: Paint the edge of a live paint group nearest a point with a colour.

cmd:magicWand.options.label: Magic Wand Settings
cmd:magicWand.options.desc: Report the current magic wand tolerance settings.

cmd:magicWand.set.label: Magic Wand Options
cmd:magicWand.set.params: {fillColor?, fillTolerance?: 0-255, strokeColor?, strokeTolerance?: 0-255, strokeWeight?, weightTolerance?: pt, opacity?, opacityTolerance?: %, blendingMode?, reset?: bool} → the settings
cmd:magicWand.set.desc: Set what the magic wand matches: fill or stroke colour, weight, opacity or blend mode.
