tool:create_graph.params: {categories?:array, csv?:string, height*:number, rows?:array, series?:array, type?:string, width*:number, x*:number, y*:number}
tool:create_graph.text0: Create a graph (graph tools) in the plot rectangle. Data as `csv` (first row: empty cell then series names; then one row per category: label, values…) or `series`/`categories`/`rows`. Edit later with run_command graph.setData / graph.setType.
tool:create_graph.desc: Create a graph (graph tools) in the plot rectangle. Data as `csv` (first row: empty cell then series names; then one row per category: label, values…) or `series`/`categories`/`rows`. Edit later with run_command graph.setData / graph.setType.

tool:draw_path.text0: Create a path from points ([[x,y],…] or [{x,y,in?:[x,y],out?:[x,y]},…] with Bézier handles) or SVG path data `d`, then apply optional paint. Returns the new object id.
tool:draw_path.desc: Create a path from points ([[x,y],…] or [{x,y,in?:[x,y],out?:[x,y]},…] with Bézier handles) or SVG path data `d`, then apply optional paint. Returns the new object id.

tool:draw_shape.params: {cx?:number, cy?:number, fill?, height?:number, points?:integer, radius?:number, radius1?:number, radius2?:number, rotation?:number, shape*:string, sides?:integer, stroke?, strokeWidth?:number, width?:number, x?:number, x1?:number, x2?:number, y?:number, y1?:number, y2?:number}
tool:draw_shape.text0: Create a live shape and apply optional paint. rectangle/ellipse: x, y, width, height (rectangle: radius = corner radius). polygon: cx, cy, radius, sides. star: cx, cy, radius1, radius2, points. line: x1, y1, x2, y2. Returns the new object id.
tool:draw_shape.desc: Create a live shape and apply optional paint. rectangle/ellipse: x, y, width, height (rectangle: radius = corner radius). polygon: cx, cy, radius, sides. star: cx, cy, radius1, radius2, points. line: x1, y1, x2, y2. Returns the new object id.

tool:export.params: {artboard?:integer, format?:string, options?:object, outlineText?:boolean, path?:string, range?:string, scale?:number, selection?:boolean}
tool:export.text0: Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.
tool:export.desc: Export the active document with the engine's document.export (the same bytes in the app and headless), in any format of the `format` enum: vectors (svg/svgz with the artboard as viewBox, eps, dxf, emf, wmf), pdf (one page per artboard: all, or `artboard` / `range`), rasters (one rendered artboard: png, jpg, webp, gif, png8 as an indexed .png, tiff, bmp, tga, psd with its layers), txt (the stories, back to front), vectorcraft or template (a native copy or template; the document keeps its path). run_command document.formats lists each format's options. `selection: true` exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds. Template layers are left out; live effects are kept (geometry baked, SVG filters for shadows/glows/blur). Without `path` the bytes come back as dataBase64.

tool:inspect_document.text0: Summary of the active document: artboards, layer tree (ids, names, kinds, bounds, fill/stroke), selection, undo history, current tool and default paint. On a large document pass depth: 0 for the layer skeleton (truncated levels report childCount), then locate objects with run_command document.find and read them with document.node.
tool:inspect_document.desc: Summary of the active document: artboards, layer tree (ids, names, kinds, bounds, fill/stroke), selection, undo history, current tool and default paint. On a large document pass depth: 0 for the layer skeleton (truncated levels report childCount), then locate objects with run_command document.find and read them with document.node.

tool:inspect_ui.text0: UI state of the running desktop app: tool and options, panels, dialogs, view (zoom/center), window, documents, perf. Desktop app only.
tool:inspect_ui.desc: UI state of the running desktop app: tool and options, panels, dialogs, view (zoom/center), window, documents, perf. Desktop app only.

tool:invoke_menu.text0: Invoke a menu item by its command id (same ids as list_commands, including UI-only commands like view.zoomIn or window.* in the desktop app).
tool:invoke_menu.desc: Invoke a menu item by its command id (same ids as list_commands, including UI-only commands like view.zoomIn or window.* in the desktop app).

tool:list_commands.text0: List VectorCraft commands (id, label, menu path, shortcut, parameter description, enabled state). Every editing action is a command; run any of them with run_command. Coordinates are points in document space, y down, origin at the first artboard's top-left.
tool:list_commands.desc: List VectorCraft commands (id, label, menu path, shortcut, parameter description, enabled state). Every editing action is a command; run any of them with run_command. Coordinates are points in document space, y down, origin at the first artboard's top-left.

tool:open_file.text0: Open a file as a new, active document: .vectorcraft, .drawcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .ai, .ait, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .vctemplate, .dxf, .emf, .wmf, .eps (see run_command document.formats). Templates (.ait, native templates) open as a new untitled document. The reply's `warnings` say what didn't come in as it was (an EPS shown as its preview image says why its PostScript couldn't be read).
tool:open_file.desc: Open a file as a new, active document: .vectorcraft, .drawcraft, .svg, .svgz, .pdf, .ai, .ait, .png, .jpg, .jpeg, .gif, .webp, .tif, .tiff, .bmp, .vctemplate, .dxf, .emf, .wmf, .eps (see run_command document.formats). Templates (.ait, native templates) open as a new untitled document. The reply's `warnings` say what didn't come in as it was (an EPS shown as its preview image says why its PostScript couldn't be read).

tool:open_panel.text0: Open a panel in the desktop app's dock by id (layers, swatches, stroke, align, pathfinder, transform, …; case-insensitive, display labels like "Layers" work too). Desktop app only.
tool:open_panel.desc: Open a panel in the desktop app's dock by id (layers, swatches, stroke, align, pathfinder, transform, …; case-insensitive, display labels like "Layers" work too). Desktop app only.

tool:pathfinder.text0: Combine the selected (or `ids`) objects destructively, back to front: unite, minusFront, intersect, exclude, divide, trim, merge, crop, outline, minusBack. For a non-destructive version apply the pathfinder.* effect to a group.
tool:pathfinder.desc: Combine the selected (or `ids`) objects destructively, back to front: unite, minusFront, intersect, exclude, divide, trim, merge, crop, outline, minusBack. For a non-destructive version apply the pathfinder.* effect to a group.

tool:pointer_gesture.text0: Drive the active tool with mouse events in document coordinates, exactly like the mouse would (e.g. a rectangle drag: down at (100,100), drag to (200,150), up at (200,150)). Optionally selects `tool` first.
tool:pointer_gesture.desc: Drive the active tool with mouse events in document coordinates, exactly like the mouse would (e.g. a rectangle drag: down at (100,100), drag to (200,150), up at (200,150)). Optionally selects `tool` first.

tool:press_key.text0: Send a key press with modifiers, e.g. {key:"Z", mods:{cmd:true}} (undo), {key:"Escape"}, {key:"Enter"}. In the desktop app it goes through the real keyboard path; headless, it runs the command or tool bound to that shortcut.
tool:press_key.desc: Send a key press with modifiers, e.g. {key:"Z", mods:{cmd:true}} (undo), {key:"Escape"}, {key:"Enter"}. In the desktop app it goes through the real keyboard path; headless, it runs the command or tool bound to that shortcut.

tool:redo.text0: Redo the last undone change (Edit → Redo).
tool:redo.desc: Redo the last undone change (Edit → Redo).

tool:run_command.text0: Execute any VectorCraft command by id with JSON params (see list_commands for ids and params). Examples: {"command":"object.group"}, {"command":"object.align","params":{"align":"left"}}, {"command":"file.new","params":{"width":800,"height":600}}. Returns the command's result (e.g. {id} for creation commands).
tool:run_command.desc: Execute any VectorCraft command by id with JSON params (see list_commands for ids and params). Examples: {"command":"object.group"}, {"command":"object.align","params":{"align":"left"}}, {"command":"file.new","params":{"width":800,"height":600}}. Returns the command's result (e.g. {id} for creation commands).

tool:save_file.text0: Save the active document with the engine's document.save: by default to its own file in its own format (native .vectorcraft unless it was opened from or saved as SVG, PDF or a restorable .ai). With `path`, the extension picks the format: .vectorcraft, .vctemplate, .pdf, .svg, .svgz, .ai. Other formats are exports (see export). The reply's `format` says what was written and `warnings` what that format loses.
tool:save_file.desc: Save the active document with the engine's document.save: by default to its own file in its own format (native .vectorcraft unless it was opened from or saved as SVG, PDF or a restorable .ai). With `path`, the extension picks the format: .vectorcraft, .vctemplate, .pdf, .svg, .svgz, .ai. Other formats are exports (see export). The reply's `format` says what was written and `warnings` what that format loses.

tool:screenshot.text0: Render the active artboard to PNG and return it as an image (optionally also saving it to `path`). With window:true (desktop app only) captures the whole app window instead.
tool:screenshot.desc: Render the active artboard to PNG and return it as an image (optionally also saving it to `path`). With window:true (desktop app only) captures the whole app window instead.

tool:select_tool.text0: Switch the active tool (as clicking it in the Tools panel). Ids: selection, directSelection, groupSelection, pen, rectangle, roundedRectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, lineSegment, …
tool:select_tool.desc: Switch the active tool (as clicking it in the Tools panel). Ids: selection, directSelection, groupSelection, pen, rectangle, roundedRectangle, ellipse, polygon, star, lineSegment, …

tool:set_paint.text0: Set fill, stroke and/or stroke weight on the selection (or `ids`) and as the default for new art.
tool:set_paint.desc: Set fill, stroke and/or stroke weight on the selection (or `ids`) and as the default for new art.

tool:text_wrap.text0: Make the selected (or `ids`) objects wrap objects: area type below them in the same layer flows around them (offset in pt, invert = flow inside). `release: true` removes the wrap.
tool:text_wrap.desc: Make the selected (or `ids`) objects wrap objects: area type below them in the same layer flows around them (offset in pt, invert = flow inside). `release: true` removes the wrap.

tool:transform.params: {copy?:boolean, dx?:number, dy?:number, ids?:array, origin?:array, reflect?:string, rotate?:number, scale?:number, scaleX?:number, scaleY?:number, shear?:number}
tool:transform.text0: Move, rotate, scale, reflect or shear the selection (or `ids`); several may be combined and run in that order. Angles in degrees (counter-clockwise), scale in %. `origin` [x,y] defaults to the selection centre; `copy` transforms a copy.
tool:transform.desc: Move, rotate, scale, reflect or shear the selection (or `ids`); several may be combined and run in that order. Angles in degrees (counter-clockwise), scale in %. `origin` [x,y] defaults to the selection centre; `copy` transforms a copy.

tool:type_text.text0: Type text into the focused widget (text tool, dialog field). Desktop app only.
tool:type_text.desc: Type text into the focused widget (text tool, dialog field). Desktop app only.

note:no-new-document-tool.label: Creating a document and drawing in VectorCraft
note:no-new-document-tool.text0: There is no new_document tool: run file.new {width, height, title} (craftmcp.py new vectorcraft width=600 height=500 title=X). Draw with draw_shape {shape: rectangle|ellipse|polygon|star|line, fill/stroke as '#rrggbb', strokeWidth} and draw_path {points or SVG d}; objects stack in creation order. For many objects write a Python script that calls the tools instead of one command per object.
note:no-new-document-tool.desc: There is no new_document tool: run file.new {width, height, title} (craftmcp.py new vectorcraft width=600 height=500 title=X). Draw with draw_shape {shape: rectangle|ellipse|polygon|star|line, fill/stroke as '#rrggbb', strokeWidth} and draw_path {points or SVG d}; objects stack in creation order. For many objects write a Python script that calls the tools instead of one command per object.

cmd:app.home.label: Home
cmd:app.home.params: {} shows the Home screen (new file presets, Open) over the open documents; choosing a document tab returns to it
cmd:app.home.desc: Show the Home screen with new-file presets and Open over the open documents.

cmd:app.language.label: Interface Language
cmd:app.language.params: {lang: auto|<code>} the interface language, persisted as the `interfaceLanguage` preference (`auto` follows the system locale; codes: prefs.list › interfaceLanguage, e.g. en, ja, cs, es, zh-hant)
cmd:app.language.desc: Change the interface language, following the system locale automatically or picking a code.

cmd:artboard.copy.label: Copy Artboard
cmd:artboard.copy.params: {index?, art?} (defaults as artboard.duplicate) put the artboard, and the art fully inside it when `art`, on the clipboard: edit.paste adds a copy right of the last artboard, edit.pasteInPlace/InFront/InBack where it was, in this or another document (one undo step; edit.pasteOnAllArtboards pastes only the art); edit.copy runs this while the Artboard tool is chosen → {copied: objects}
cmd:artboard.copy.desc: Copy an artboard, with its art if wanted, to the clipboard for pasting here or elsewhere.

cmd:artboard.cut.label: Cut Artboard
cmd:artboard.cut.params: {index?, art?} artboard.copy, then delete the artboard and that art in one undo step (not the only artboard); edit.cut runs this while the Artboard tool is chosen → {copied: objects}
cmd:artboard.cut.desc: Cut an artboard and its art to the clipboard, deleting both in one undo step.

cmd:assets.add.label: Collect for Export
cmd:assets.add.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selected objects), multiple?: true (an asset per object; false: one asset of them all), name?: (the asset's name, when it makes one)} collect art as assets for Window › Asset Export and Export for Screens' Assets tab, named after the object (else Asset 1, Asset 2…); art already collected as such an asset keeps it → {assets: [asset id…] (in order), added: n}. Assets follow their art: moving it moves the crop, deleting it removes it from the asset
cmd:assets.add.desc: Collect selected art as named assets ready for the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens.

cmd:assets.export.label: Export Assets
cmd:assets.export.params: {assets?: [asset id…] (default all), folder?, zip?, openLocation?, formats?, preset?, settings?, prefix?, subfolders?, antiAlias?} each asset's art alone, cropped to it, in every format row: document.exportForScreens {assets} at the document's export settings (document.exportSettings) under the ones given → what document.exportForScreens returns (no folder: the files, or one zip, as dataBase64). Leaves the remembered settings as they are (assets.settings.set changes them)
cmd:assets.export.desc: Export each asset's art cropped on its own in every chosen file format.

cmd:assets.list.label: Assets
cmd:assets.list.params: {} → {assets: [{id, name, nodes: [id…], bounds: [x, y, width, height] | null (the crop: the visual bounds of its art)}]} the Asset Export panel's assets, in order
cmd:assets.list.desc: List the Asset Export panel's assets with names, artwork and crop bounds.

cmd:assets.remove.label: Remove Asset
cmd:assets.remove.params: {assets: [asset id…]} take assets out of the Asset Export panel (their art stays) → {removed: n}
cmd:assets.remove.desc: Remove assets from the Asset Export panel while keeping their artwork.

cmd:assets.rename.label: Rename Asset
cmd:assets.rename.params: {asset: id, name} rename an asset (its files' names)
cmd:assets.rename.desc: Rename an asset, changing the names of its exported files.

cmd:assets.settings.set.label: Asset Export Settings
cmd:assets.settings.set.params: {formats?, preset?: mobile|density|"" (none), settings?, prefix?, subfolders?, antiAlias?} change the export settings the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens share (document.exportSettings; the values of document.exportForScreens; null removes one): formats replace a preset, a preset replaces the formats → {settings}. Not an undo step
cmd:assets.settings.set.desc: Set the export formats and options shared by the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens.

cmd:clipboard.conflicts.label: Swatch Conflicts
cmd:clipboard.conflicts.params: {} → {swatches: [{name, document, clipboard, spot}]} the global or spot swatches the copied objects use whose name the active document gives another colour (`document`/`clipboard`: #rrggbb): Paste asks Merge or Add for each (pass the answer as edit.paste* {swatchConflict}). Pasting back into the document the objects came from raises none
cmd:clipboard.conflicts.desc: List copied swatches whose names clash with different colours in the active document.

cmd:clipboard.exportPdf.label: Clipboard as PDF
cmd:clipboard.exportPdf.params: {} → {dataBase64} a one-page PDF of the copied objects, the page their visual bounds (null when the clipboard is empty)
cmd:clipboard.exportPdf.desc: Export the copied objects as a one-page PDF sized to their bounds.

cmd:clipboard.exportPng.label: Clipboard as PNG
cmd:clipboard.exportPng.params: {scale?: 1 (pixels per point, up to 64)} → {dataBase64, width, height (px)} the copied objects cropped to their visual bounds, transparent around them (dataBase64 null when the clipboard is empty)
cmd:clipboard.exportPng.desc: Export the copied objects as a transparent PNG cropped to their bounds at a chosen scale.

cmd:clipboard.exportText.label: Clipboard as Text
cmd:clipboard.exportText.params: {} → {text} the copied type objects' text, one object per line (null unless every copied object is type, or a group of type)
cmd:clipboard.exportText.desc: Export the copied text objects' words as plain text, one object per line.

cmd:clipboard.flavours.label: Clipboard Formats
cmd:clipboard.flavours.params: {} → {flavours: [mime…]} what Copy offers other apps for the current clipboard, best first, by the Clipboard Handling preferences: text/plain (a type-only copy's text, else the SVG markup with copyAsSvg), image/svg+xml (copyAsSvg), application/pdf (copyAsPdf), image/png (always; PDF and PNG only for objects with an area); the app publishes them on Copy and Cut
cmd:clipboard.flavours.desc: List the formats the current clipboard offers other apps, best first.

cmd:clipboard.importEmf.label: Load Metafile into Clipboard
cmd:clipboard.importEmf.params: {dataBase64 (EMF or WMF bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the picture's objects (paths, clipping groups, images, point type; the images they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; records VectorCraft doesn't read are skipped with one warning; then run edit.paste
cmd:clipboard.importEmf.desc: Replace the clipboard with the objects of an EMF or WMF metafile picture.

cmd:clipboard.importImage.label: Load Image into Clipboard
cmd:clipboard.importImage.params: {dataBase64 (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes), mime?: the type the system clipboard gave (an image/… type; the format is read from the bytes), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the image, embedded at 100% of its physical size (its resolution, else 72 ppi), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, width, height (pt), pixelWidth, pixelHeight}; then run edit.paste
cmd:clipboard.importImage.desc: Replace the clipboard with a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP image for pasting.

cmd:clipboard.importPdf.label: Load PDF into Clipboard
cmd:clipboard.importPdf.params: {dataBase64, page?: 1, password? (an encrypted PDF), center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with the objects of one PDF page (with the images, patterns and swatches they use), centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count, warnings}; then run edit.paste
cmd:clipboard.importPdf.desc: Replace the clipboard with one PDF page's objects, ready to paste.

cmd:clipboard.importText.label: Load Text into Clipboard
cmd:clipboard.importText.params: {text, center?: [x, y]} replace the clipboard with point text of `text` (one paragraph per line; trailing line breaks dropped) in the default type style, centred on `center` (default: the first artboard) → {count}; then run edit.paste
cmd:clipboard.importText.desc: Replace the clipboard with point text built from a string, ready to paste.

cmd:css.copy.label: Copy Selected Style
cmd:css.copy.params: {scope?: selection|all (default selection), …css.selection options} copy the CSS of the selection (css.selection; all: css.generate) to the clipboard (CSS Properties panel) → {css, rules: n}
cmd:css.copy.desc: Copy the selection's CSS styles to the clipboard for use in web pages.

cmd:css.export.label: Export CSS
cmd:css.export.params: {path?, scope?: selection|all (default selection; ids? picks the objects), …css.selection options} write the CSS (css.selection, or css.generate for all) to path and, with rasterize, each picture its rules refer to next to it (PNG of the object's visual bounds, 1 px per point) → {path, bytes, rules: n, images: [path…], warnings}; no path → {data: the CSS, name: <document>.css, rules, images: [{name, dataBase64}], warnings}
cmd:css.export.desc: Write the document's or selection's CSS to a file, with any pictures it references.

cmd:css.exportFile.label: Export CSS…
cmd:css.exportFile.params: {path?, scope?: selection|all (default selection), …css.selection options} css.export written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it), with the pictures of rasterized art next to it (CSS Properties panel: Export Selected CSS…, Export All…) → {path, rules, images: [path…]}
cmd:css.exportFile.desc: Export CSS to a chosen file, saving pictures of rasterized art beside it.

cmd:css.generate.label: Generate CSS
cmd:css.generate.params: {…css.selection options} css.selection of every object in the document
cmd:css.generate.desc: Generate CSS code for every object in the document.

cmd:css.selection.label: CSS Properties
cmd:css.selection.params: {ids?: [id…] (default: the selection), units?: px|pt|mm|cm|in (default px; 1 px = 1 pt, as in SVG export), position?: false (position: absolute, left and top from the artboard's top-left), dimensions?: true (width, height), unnamed?: true (unnamed objects too, classes named after their kind; false: named objects only), rasterize?: false (art CSS can't describe as background-image: url(<class>.png), its picture, which css.export writes)} the CSS web pages style the objects with, one rule per object back to front (layers and plain groups stand for what they hold): a rectangle's or ellipse's fill as background-color or linear-/radial-gradient(), stroke as border, corners as border-radius; type's font, color, spacing and alignment; opacity, mix-blend-mode, shadows and glows (box-shadow, text-shadow), blur (filter) → {css, rules: [{id, selector, css, unsupported?: why CSS can't describe the art exactly (without rasterize it is written as its box), image?: the PNG it refers to}], skipped: n unnamed objects left out, warnings}
cmd:css.selection.desc: Return the CSS properties of the chosen objects, with units, position and dimension options.

cmd:docInfo.save.label: Save Document Info…
cmd:docInfo.save.params: {path?, selectionOnly?} write Document Info's text report (document.info {format: "text"}) to path, else a picked file (the web downloads it) → {path}
cmd:docInfo.save.desc: Save the Document Info report as a text file.

cmd:document.dxfInfo.label: DXF Info
cmd:document.dxfInfo.params: {path} or {name?, dataBase64} what a DXF drawing holds → {version (2018, R12…), units (its drawing unit: Millimeters, Inches, Unitless…), layouts: ["Model", paper layouts…], layers: [name…], unit, scale (the default ratio: 1 unit = scale drawing units, the drawing at 1:1)}; a binary DXF or a DWG answers an error saying to save it as ASCII DXF
cmd:document.dxfInfo.desc: Report what a DXF drawing contains: version, units, layouts and layers.

cmd:document.exportDxf.label: Export DXF
cmd:document.exportDxf.params: {path?, version?: R12|R13|R14|2000|2004|2007|2010|2013|2018 (default), unit?: mm (default; any unit name: pt, in, cm…), scale?: 1 (drawing units per unit), scaleLineweights?: false, colors?: 8|16|256|true (default; true colour needs 2004+, else 256), rasterFormat?: png (default)|jpeg (placed images, written next to the file), preserve?: appearance (default: type as outlines; strokes a CAD line can't draw as filled outlines; brush art)|editability (type as text; every stroke a line with its lineweight and dashes), alterPaths?: false (every stroke as its filled outline), outlineText?: false, selectedOnly?: false (the selected objects, in their layers), artboard?: 0 (the origin is its bottom-left corner), useArtboards?: true (one drawing per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, holding the art over it: {stem}-{artboard}.dxf) | false (the origin at the art's bounds)} → {path, bytes, warnings, files?, linked?: [image files]}; no path → {dataBase64, …, linked?: [{name, dataBase64}]}. Layers become DXF layers (hidden: off; locked; non-printing: not plotted); paths become polylines and splines, fills solid hatches. Same as document.export {format: dxf}
cmd:document.exportDxf.desc: Export the document as a DXF CAD drawing with chosen version, units and colour depth.

cmd:document.exportEps.label: Export EPS
cmd:document.exportEps.params: {path?, level?: 2|3 (default; PostScript language level: 3 writes smooth gradients and masks transparent image pixels out, 2 steps gradients and writes those pixels white), previewFormat?: none|tiffBw|tiffColor (default: a TIFF preview other apps show), transparentPreview?: true (else on white), overprints?: preserve (default)|discard, flattenerPreset?: "medium" (default; high, low or a saved preset: flattener.presets.list), flattener?: {the options of object.flattenTransparency over the preset}, embedFonts?: true (type is always written as outlines, so no fonts are needed), includeLinkedFiles?: false (the embedded document keeps linked images whole, not just their previews), thumbnails?: true (a PNG thumbnail in the file), cmykPostScript?: true (RGB documents written in CMYK), compatibleGradients?: false (stepped gradients at level 3 too), selectedOnly?: false, useArtboards?: true (one file per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, {stem}_{artboard}.eps, the bounding box the artboard) | false (default: one file, the bounding box the visible art, y up from the first artboard's bottom-left corner)} → {path, bytes, warnings, files?}; no path → {dataBase64, …}. Transparency is flattened with the preset (EPS has none); the native document rides along in comments, for reopening the file as it was. Same as document.export {format: eps}
cmd:document.exportEps.desc: Export the document as EPS PostScript with a preview image for other applications.

cmd:document.exportForOffice.label: Save for Office Documents…
cmd:document.exportForOffice.params: {path?, ppi?: 150 (72, 150, 300… pixels per inch), transparent?: false (else on white), artboard?: 0} the artboard as a PNG for office documents and slides → {path, bytes, width, height} (pixels); no path → {dataBase64, bytes, width, height}
cmd:document.exportForOffice.desc: Save the artboard as a PNG sized for office documents and slides.

cmd:document.exportForWeb.label: Save for Web
cmd:document.exportForWeb.params: {path?, preset?: a webExport.presets name (its settings, then these keys), format?: gif (default)|jpg|png8|png24, gif/png8: reduction?: perceptual|selective (default)|adaptive|web|blackWhite|gray, colors?: 128 (2–256), dither?: none|diffusion (default)|pattern|noise, ditherAmount?: 100, webSnap?: 0 (0–100 %: colours that close to a web-safe one become it), lossy?: 0 (0–100, gif), colorTable?: {locked?: ["#rrggbb"…] (kept when reducing), transparent?: ["#rrggbb"…] (become transparent), webShift?: ["#rrggbb"…] (become web-safe), sort?: none|hue|luminance|popularity} (colours as the preview's colors[].source), transparency?: true (gif/png8/png24), matte?: white (default)|black|none|"#rrggbb" (what edges blend into; jpg and opaque png24: the background), interlaced?: false (gif/png8/png24), jpg: quality?: 60 (0–100), progressive?: false, optimized?: true, embedProfile?: false (sRGB profile), width?: px | height?: px | percent?: 100 (the image size, proportional; width wins over height, height over percent), antiAlias?: none|art (default)|type, clipToArtboard?: true (the artboard; false: the art and the slices), artboard?: 0 (0-based), convertToSrgb?: true (PNG files say they are sRGB), metadata?: none|copyright (default)|contact|all (File Info written as PNG text, a GIF or JPEG comment), slices?: all (default)|selected|none (one image per slice: images/<slice name>.<ext>), output?: images (default)|html (an HTML page placing the image or slices, <stem>.html)} → {path, files: [path…], bytes (total), width, height}; no path → {files: [{name, dataBase64}], bytes, width, height} (names such as page.html, images/page_01.gif). A single image without HTML is written at path itself
cmd:document.exportForWeb.desc: Export the artwork as an optimized GIF, JPEG or PNG for websites.

cmd:document.exportForWeb.preview.label: Save for Web Preview
cmd:document.exportForWeb.preview.params: {…the settings of document.exportForWeb (preset?, format?…), slice?: n (1-based, from slice.list; default the whole image), kbps?: 56.6 (connection speed for the download time), image?: false (also the optimised file as dataBase64)} what Save writes for the whole image (or one slice) → {format, width, height, bytes (exactly the file's size), seconds (to download at kbps), kbps, colors?: [{color: "#rrggbb", source: "#rrggbb" (the colour the reduction made, as colorTable lists it), transparent, locked, webShifted, webSafe}] (gif/png8: the colour table in file order), mappedToTransparent?: ["#rrggbb"…], slices: images an export writes, dataBase64?}
cmd:document.exportForWeb.preview.desc: Preview the optimized web file, its size and download time before saving.

cmd:document.exportSettings.label: Export for Screens Settings
cmd:document.exportSettings.params: {} → {settings}: the document.exportForScreens params the document last exported with ({} when never; saved with the document, the dialog reopens on them)
cmd:document.exportSettings.desc: Return the export settings the document last used for Export for Screens.

cmd:document.find.label: Find Objects
cmd:document.find.params: {name?: substring of the Layers panel name, kind?: panel label such as Group, Path, Type or Image (exact), text?: substring of type content, limit?: max matches (default 100, 0 counts only)} → {matches: [{id, name, kind, path}], total}
cmd:document.find.desc: Find objects by layer name, kind or text content and list the matches.

cmd:document.pdfInfo.label: PDF Info
cmd:document.pdfInfo.params: {path} or {name?, dataBase64}, password?, thumbnail?: page (1-based), thumbnailSize?: 160 (px, longest side), cropTo?: crop (the thumbnail's box) → {pages, needsPassword, wrongPassword?, pageInfo: [{width, height (pt, as shown), rotation, boxes: {media, crop, bleed, trim, art: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (PDF space, pt)}}], thumbnail?: PNG dataBase64}; an encrypted PDF without its password → {pages: 0, needsPassword: true}
cmd:document.pdfInfo.desc: Report a PDF's pages, sizes, boxes and security, with an optional page thumbnail.

cmd:document.setup.label: Document Setup
cmd:document.setup.params: {units?: "Points"|"Inches"|"Millimeters"|…, bleed?: pt (all sides)|[top, bottom, left, right]|{top?, bottom?, left?, right?} (0–72 pt), outlineImages?: bool (show images in Outline mode), highlightSubstitutedFonts?: bool, highlightSubstitutedGlyphs?: bool, gridSize?: "small"|"medium"|"large", gridColors?: "Light"|"Medium"|"Dark"|"Red"|"Orange"|"Green"|"Blue"|"Purple"|[colour, colour] (transparency grid; the first is also the paper colour), simulatePaper?: bool, flattenerPreset?: "High Resolution"|"Medium Resolution"|"Low Resolution"|a saved preset (flattener.presets.list), discardWhiteOverprint?: bool, language?: "English: USA"|"German"|"French"|… (also picks its quotes), quotes?: {double?: "“”", single?: "‘’"} (beside a language: only if they differ from the current ones), typographersQuotes?: bool (typed straight quotes become the document's quotes), superscript?: {size?: %, position?: %}, subscript?: {size?: %, position?: %}, smallCapsSize?: %, exportText?: "editable"|"appearance" (SVG text as text or as outlines), backgroundContents?: "transparent"|"white" (white: raster exports are white behind the art)} change the document setup in one undo step; no params → the current setup
cmd:document.setup.desc: Change document units, bleed, grid and font-substitution highlighting in one dialog.

cmd:file.exportAs.label: Export As…
cmd:file.exportAs.params: {format?, useArtboards?, range?} opens Export As (then the format's options); with {path, …document.export options} writes the file(s) → {path, warnings, files?}
cmd:file.exportAs.desc: Open Export As to pick a format and options, or write the file directly.

cmd:file.exportSelection.label: Export Selection…
cmd:file.exportSelection.params: {multiple?: true} collect the selected objects as assets (assets.add: one per object; false: one of them all) and open Export for Screens on its Assets tab with them checked → {assets: [asset id…]}; document.exportSelection exports the selection in one go instead
cmd:file.exportSelection.desc: Collect selected objects as assets and open Export for Screens ready to export them.

cmd:file.formatOptions.desc: Report a file format's extensions, options and related save formats.

cmd:file.newPresets.label: New Document Presets
cmd:file.newPresets.params: {category?: "Recent"|"Saved"|"Mobile"|"Web"|"Print"|"Film & Video"|"Art & Illustration"|"Branding"|"Social"} the New Document presets by category (Recent: the last sizes used; Saved: the user's presets) → {categories: [{name, presets: [{name, size: "1920 × 1080 px", width: pt, height: pt, units, orientation, artboards, artboardLayout: {layout, columns, spacing, rightToLeft}, bleed, backgroundContents, colorMode, rasterEffectsPpi, previewMode}]}]}; file.new {preset: name} starts from one
cmd:file.newPresets.desc: List the New Document presets by category, from recent sizes to saved presets.

cmd:file.newPresets.delete.label: Delete Preset

cmd:file.newPresets.delete.desc: Delete a saved New Document preset from the preferences.

cmd:file.newPresets.save.label: Save Preset
cmd:file.newPresets.save.params: {name, preset?: start from this preset, …settings as file.new (default: Letter in prefs unitsGeneral)} save New Document settings as a user preset (the Saved category; same name = replace) in the preferences → {name, count}
cmd:file.newPresets.save.desc: Save current new-document settings as a named user preset.

cmd:file.package.label: Package
cmd:file.package.params: {folder?, name?: (default: "<document> Folder"), copyLinks?: true, linksFolder?: true (the linked files go in Links/, else next to the document), relink?: true (the packaged document links to the copies), copyFonts?: true (the fonts its type uses go in Fonts/; fonts whose licence doesn't allow embedding are left out), report?: true (<document> Report.txt)} copy the saved document as it is now into folder/name as <document>.vectorcraft with its linked files and fonts; the open document doesn't change → {folder, files: [paths relative to folder/name], links, fonts (counts copied), missingLinks: [file names not found], skippedFonts: [{font, reason}]}; no folder → the same with {name: "<name>.zip", dataBase64} (a zip of the files in <name>/) instead of folder
