cmd:file.place.info.label: Placed File Info
cmd:file.place.info.params: {path | name+dataBase64, page?, crop?, password?, thumbnail?: px} what file.place would place, without placing it → {name, format, width, height (pt at 100%), pixelWidth?, pixelHeight?, ppi?: [x, y], colorMode?: RGB|Grayscale|CMYK (raster images), warnings, thumbnailBase64?: PNG of at most `thumbnail` (≤ 512) px on its longer side}
cmd:file.place.info.desc: Report what placing a file would bring in: format, size, resolution and colour mode, without placing.

cmd:file.place.queue.label: Load Place Cursor
cmd:file.place.queue.params: {paths?: [path…], files?: [{name, dataBase64}…], link?, template?, page?, crop?, text?, dxf?, thumbnail?: px} load the place cursor (the `place` tool) with up to 100 files (as file.place reads them): a click places the current file at 100% with its top-left corner there, a drag places it at the dragged size (aspect kept), ←/→ and ↑/↓ cycle the files, Esc discards the current one; each placement is a file.place, and the previous tool returns after the last → {count, files: [{name, format, width, height, thumbnailBase64?}], skipped: [{name, error}]}
cmd:file.place.queue.desc: Load the place cursor with files so each click places the next one.

cmd:file.print.label: Print…
cmd:file.print.params: {} open the Print dialog (dialog `print`: the print.setup settings, preset (setting it loads that print preset; Save Preset… saves them as one), printer, toFile; Print keeps the settings with the document and prints, Done (discard: true) only keeps them); with params {settings? (over the document's), printer? (print.printers name; "" the default), toFile?, path?, format?: pdf|postscript, level?, flattenerPreset? (as engine file.print)} print without it: the print-ready PDF (engine file.print) goes to the printer → {pages, printer, printed: true, warnings}; with toFile, a path or no printing here (no print service) it is saved as a PDF at path (else a picked file, the web downloads it) → {path, pages, printed: false, warnings}; a PostScript file (format postscript, or a .ps path) is always saved that way
cmd:file.print.desc: Open the Print dialog to choose printer, presets and settings, then print.

cmd:file.recovery.discard.label: Discard Recovered Documents
cmd:file.recovery.discard.params: {file?} delete a copy left behind by a crash (default: every one; copies of open documents and of running VectorCraft apps stay) → {discarded: [file…]}
cmd:file.recovery.discard.desc: Delete the recovery copies left behind by a crash.

cmd:file.recovery.list.label: Recovery Data
cmd:file.recovery.list.params: {} the recovery copies in the store → {copies: [{file ("<area>/<name>"), title, path (the document's file, if it had one), format, saved (Unix seconds or null), open (the copy of a document open here), running (kept by another VectorCraft that is running)}], location}; copies neither open nor running were left behind by a crash
cmd:file.recovery.list.desc: List the recovery copies in the store with their documents and save times.

cmd:file.recovery.restore.label: Restore Recovered Documents
cmd:file.recovery.restore.params: {file?} open a copy left behind by a crash (default: every one; a running VectorCraft's copies are never taken) as a new document titled "<name> [Recovered]": modified, and Save asks where to save it (suggesting its original file) → {restored: [{index, title, file, path, warnings, missingLinks, modifiedLinks, updatedLinks}], failed: [{file, error}] (damaged copies, when restoring every one; a named one fails the command)}. The copy moves to this app's area and stays until the document is saved or closed
cmd:file.recovery.restore.desc: Reopen documents recovered after a crash as new modified copies.

cmd:file.recovery.save.label: Save Recovery Data
cmd:file.recovery.save.params: {} write a recovery copy of every modified document changed since its last copy, in this app's own area of the store (the app does this every autosaveInterval minutes while autosaveRecovery is on; documents of more than 20000 objects are skipped while recoveryOffForComplex is on). A copy goes when its document is saved, reverted or closed → {saved: [{file, title, bytes}], skipped: [{title, reason}], location} (location: the recovery folder, or browser storage on the web)
cmd:file.recovery.save.desc: Save recovery copies of every modified document so crashes lose little work.

cmd:file.reveal.label: Show in Folder
cmd:file.reveal.params: {} show the document's file in the system file manager (desktop) → {path}
cmd:file.reveal.desc: Show the document's file in the system file manager.

cmd:file.saveForWeb.label: Save for Web (Legacy)…
cmd:file.saveForWeb.params: {} open Save for Web (dialog `saveForWeb`: fields = the webExport.settings settings, `preset` loads a preset, __view: original|optimized|2up|4up, __zoom, __kbps; Save… remembers the settings and writes the files, Done only remembers them); with settings = document.exportForWeb, written to path, else a picked file (the web downloads the files) → {path, files, bytes}
cmd:file.saveForWeb.desc: Open the Save for Web dialog to optimize and export images for the web.

cmd:file.saveForWeb.browser.label: Preview in Browser
cmd:file.saveForWeb.browser.params: {…document.exportForWeb settings} write the HTML page and its images to a temporary folder and open the page in the default browser (desktop) → {path}
cmd:file.saveForWeb.browser.desc: Write the web page and its images to a temporary folder and open the page in your browser.

cmd:file.showPackage.label: Show Package
cmd:file.showPackage.params: {folder} show a package folder (file.package's folder) in the file manager → {folder}
cmd:file.showPackage.desc: Show a package folder in the system file manager.

cmd:guide.list.label: Guides
cmd:guide.list.params: {} → [{index, vertical, pos, selected, artboard?: index (an artboard guide's)}…] the ruler guides
cmd:guide.list.desc: List the ruler guides with positions, orientation and selection.

cmd:guide.select.label: Select Guides
cmd:guide.select.params: {indexes: [index…], toggle?: bool} select ruler guides on their own (deselecting the art); toggle adds or removes them instead → {selected: [index…]}
cmd:guide.select.desc: Select ruler guides on their own, adding or toggling as needed.

cmd:image.info.label: Image Info
cmd:image.info.params: {id?} an image object (default: the one selected) → {id, name, linked, link, colorMode: RGB|Grayscale|CMYK, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, ppi: [x, y] at its placed size, width, height}
cmd:image.info.desc: Report an image's link, colour mode, pixel size and resolution.

cmd:layer.flatten.label: Flatten Artwork
cmd:layer.flatten.params: {id?} (default: the highlighted row's top-level layer, else the current one's) move the art of every other visible top-level layer into this one, keeping the stacking order; hidden layers and their art are deleted, template layers stay. One undo step → {id, discarded}
cmd:layer.flatten.desc: Merge every visible top-level layer's art into one layer, deleting hidden layers.

cmd:layer.hideOthers.label: Hide Others
cmd:layer.hideOthers.params: {ids?} hide every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer). One undo step → {count}
cmd:layer.hideOthers.desc: Hide every top-level layer except the chosen ones.

cmd:layer.highlight.label: Highlight Rows
cmd:layer.highlight.params: {ids, mode?: "set"|"add"|"toggle"} highlight Layers panel rows (Shift-click: a range, Ctrl-click: toggle one); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step → {rows}
cmd:layer.highlight.desc: Highlight Layers panel rows like clicking, making the last layer current.

cmd:layer.locate.label: Locate Object
cmd:layer.locate.params: {id?} (default: the last selected object) highlight the object's row; the Layers panel opens the layers around it and scrolls to it → {id, ancestry: [layer…, id]}
cmd:layer.locate.desc: Scroll the Layers panel to an object and highlight its row.

cmd:layer.lockOthers.label: Lock Others
cmd:layer.lockOthers.params: {ids?} lock every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer) → {count}
cmd:layer.lockOthers.desc: Lock every top-level layer except the chosen ones.

cmd:layer.merge.label: Merge Selected
cmd:layer.merge.params: {ids?} (default: the highlighted rows) merge two or more rows into the layer listed (highlighted) last: the other layers' contents and the other rows move into it, keeping their stacking order, and the emptied layers go. One undo step → {id}
cmd:layer.merge.desc: Merge highlighted layer rows into the last one, keeping stacking order.

cmd:layer.move.label: Move Rows
cmd:layer.move.params: {ids, target, place?: "above"|"below"|"inside" (default inside), copy?: bool} drag rows in the Layers panel: above or below the target row (beside it, in its layer or group), or inside a layer or group (on top of its contents). Layers go only in layers or at the top level, objects in layers and groups; an object placed beside a top-level layer goes inside it. A row never goes into itself; a locked layer or group takes nothing. `copy` (Alt-drag) moves copies. One undo step → {ids}
cmd:layer.move.desc: Move or copy Layers panel rows above, below or inside another row.

cmd:layer.outlineOthers.label: Outline Others
cmd:layer.outlineOthers.params: {ids?} turn Preview off (outline view) for every top-level layer but those holding the highlighted rows (else the current layer) → {count}
cmd:layer.outlineOthers.desc: Switch every top-level layer except the chosen ones to outline view.

cmd:layer.pasteRemembersLayers.label: Paste Remembers Layers
cmd:layer.pasteRemembersLayers.params: {on?} (default: toggle) the document option: on, the Paste commands put objects back into the layers they were copied from (by name; a missing one is made on top), off into the current layer; one undo step when it changes (document.inspect → pasteRemembersLayers) → {on}
cmd:layer.pasteRemembersLayers.desc: Toggle whether pasted objects return to the layers they were copied from.

cmd:layer.previewAll.label: Preview All Layers
cmd:layer.previewAll.params: {} turn Preview on for every layer and sublayer → {count}
cmd:layer.previewAll.desc: Turn preview mode back on for every layer and sublayer.

cmd:layer.releaseToLayers.label: Release to Layers (Sequence)
cmd:layer.releaseToLayers.params: {id?: layer or group (default: the highlighted row, else the current layer), build?: bool} each object in it goes into a new sublayer of its own, in stacking order (a group's objects go into sublayers of its layer, where the group was). `build`: Release to Layers (Build), each new sublayer holds copies of the objects up to its own, so the layers add up. One undo step → {ids}
cmd:layer.releaseToLayers.desc: Move each object in a layer or group into its own new sublayer in stacking order.

cmd:layer.releaseToLayersBuild.label: Release to Layers (Build)
cmd:layer.releaseToLayersBuild.desc: Release each object into its own sublayer, building them up cumulatively.

cmd:layer.reverse.label: Reverse Order
cmd:layer.reverse.params: {ids?} (default: the highlighted rows) reverse the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group; each keeps the places the others held. One undo step
cmd:layer.reverse.desc: Reverse the stacking order of rows sharing a layer or group.

cmd:layer.showAll.label: Show All Layers
cmd:layer.showAll.desc: Show every hidden layer and sublayer at once.

cmd:layer.template.label: Template
cmd:layer.template.params: {ids?, on?: bool (default: toggle the first)} make layers templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or ordinary layers again (layer.setProps template) → {on}
cmd:layer.template.desc: Make layers dimmed, locked templates for tracing, or turn them back to normal.

cmd:layer.unlockAll.label: Unlock All Layers
cmd:layer.unlockAll.desc: Unlock every locked layer and sublayer at once.

cmd:links.check.label: Check Links
cmd:links.check.params: {ids?: [image ids] (default: every linked image)} where each linked file is and whether it changed since it was read → {links: [{name, path, status: ok|modified|missing, ids, found?: path (found away from its path: relative to the document, or by name in its folder), preview: true (showing the low-resolution preview, not the file)}], missing, modified}
cmd:links.check.desc: Report where each linked file is and whether it changed or went missing.

cmd:links.editOriginal.label: Edit Original
cmd:links.editOriginal.params: {id?} open the file of linked image `id` (default: the selected linked image) in the system's default app for its type (Links panel, Edit › Edit Original) → {path}; edits saved there show after links.update
cmd:links.editOriginal.desc: Open a linked image's file in its default application for editing.

cmd:links.embed.label: Embed Image
cmd:links.embed.params: {ids?: [image ids] (default: the selected linked images)} keep the linked files' pixels in the document and drop the links (an image whose file can't be found and that shows the saved preview stays linked: relink it first). One undo step → {embedded: [ids], missing: [ids]}
cmd:links.embed.desc: Store linked images' pixels inside the document and remove the links.

cmd:links.goTo.label: Go To Link
cmd:links.goTo.params: {id?} select image `id` (default: the first selected image); the Links panel scrolls it into view → {id, bounds: [x0, y0, x1, y1]}
cmd:links.goTo.desc: Select a linked image and scroll the Links panel to it.

cmd:links.info.label: Link Info
cmd:links.info.params: {id?} an image's Link Info (default: the one selected) → image.info's fields (id, name, linked, link, colorMode, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, width, height) and status: ok|modified|missing|embedded, format, ppi: [x, y] (the file's), effectivePpi: [x, y] (at its placed size), scale: [x%, y%] (of its 100% size), rotation (degrees, counter-clockwise), placement: {preserve, align, clip}; linked images also fileName, location (its folder), page?, fileSize? (bytes), modified?, created? (ms since the Unix epoch)
cmd:links.info.desc: Report a link's status, format, resolution and placed size.

cmd:links.list.label: Links
cmd:links.list.params: {show?: all (default)|missing|modified|embedded, sort?: name|kind (file format)|status (missing, modified, ok, embedded); default: stacking order, top first} every image object in the layers, as the Links panel lists them → {links: [{id, name, linked, status: ok|modified|missing|embedded, format, pixelWidth, pixelHeight, path?, found?: path (found away from its path), page?, preview?: true (showing the saved preview)}], missing, modified, embedded}
cmd:links.list.desc: List every image object as the Links panel shows it, filterable and sortable.

cmd:links.placementOptions.label: Placement Options
cmd:links.placementOptions.params: {ids?: [image ids] (default: the selected images), preserve?: transforms|bounds (default)|fileDimensions|fit|fill, align?: topLeft|top|topRight|left|center (default)|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight (where the new art sits; not for bounds), clip?: false (clip it to the old bounds where it is larger)} how a file read again (links.relink, links.update) takes each image's place: transforms keeps its scale (relative to each file's 100% size), rotation and position; bounds stretches it into the old bounds; fileDimensions puts it at 100%, unrotated; fit and fill scale it proportionally to fit inside or cover the old bounds. Without options → {placement} of the first image; else one undo step → {ids, placement}
cmd:links.placementOptions.desc: Choose how newly placed or updated images fit, align and clip.

cmd:links.relink.label: Relink
cmd:links.relink.params: {ids?: [image ids] (default: the selected images; with folder and nothing selected, every missing link), path | folder} link images to the file at path, or each to the file of its link's name in folder; embedded images become linked; each keeps its bounds. One undo step → {relinked: [ids], notFound: [file names]}
cmd:links.relink.desc: Point images at a new file, or at same-named files in a folder.

cmd:links.reveal.label: Show in Folder
cmd:links.reveal.params: {id?} show the file of linked image `id` (default: the selected linked image) in the system's file manager → {path}
cmd:links.reveal.desc: Show a linked image's file in the system file manager.

cmd:links.unembed.label: Unembed
cmd:links.unembed.params: {id?: an embedded image (default: the one selected), path?} write the image's pixels to the file at path (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP as stored, other images as PNG; a path ending in .png/.jpg/.jpeg/.gif/.webp/.tif/.tiff/.bmp converts them) and link the image to it, keeping its bounds. One undo step → {id, path}; no path → {name, dataBase64} (nothing changes: there is no file to link to)
cmd:links.unembed.desc: Save an embedded image as a file and link the image to it.

cmd:links.update.label: Update Links
cmd:links.update.params: {ids?: [image ids] (default: the linked images whose file was modified or is showing its preview)} read their linked files again; each image keeps its bounds. One undo step → {updated: [ids], missing: [ids]}
cmd:links.update.desc: Reload linked files that changed, keeping each image's size and place.

cmd:object.blend.info.label: Blend Info
cmd:object.blend.info.params: {} the options of the first selected blend, else those new blends start with → {target: blend|defaults, id?, spacing: smooth|steps|distance, steps, distance, orientation: page|path, keys?: [ids], starts?: [anchor|null], spine?: {anchors: [{x, y, in: [x, y], out: [x, y]}], closed, keyAnchors: [anchor each key sits on] | null (keys spread evenly: a spine from Replace Spine), explicit: false for the straight lines between the key centres}}
cmd:object.blend.info.desc: Report a blend's spacing, steps, orientation, key objects and spine.

cmd:object.blend.spine.addAnchor.label: Add Spine Point
cmd:object.blend.spine.addAnchor.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), x, y} add a point to the blend's spine where it passes nearest (x, y) → {anchor}
cmd:object.blend.spine.addAnchor.desc: Add a point to a blend's spine where you choose along it.

cmd:object.blend.spine.moveAnchor.label: Move Spine Point
cmd:object.blend.spine.moveAnchor.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index, x, y, handle?: in|out, independent?: bool} move a point of the blend's spine (its handles along), or with `handle` place that handle's end at (x, y) (a smooth point keeps the other handle in line unless `independent`). A key object sitting on the point moves with it. The first edit turns the straight spine into a path
cmd:object.blend.spine.moveAnchor.desc: Move a point or handle of a blend's spine to reshape the blend path.

cmd:object.blend.spine.removeAnchor.label: Delete Spine Point
cmd:object.blend.spine.removeAnchor.params: {id? (default: the selected blend), anchor: index} delete a point of the blend's spine that no key object sits on
cmd:object.blend.spine.removeAnchor.desc: Delete a spine point from a blend that no key object sits on.

cmd:object.envelope.info.label: Envelope Info
cmd:object.envelope.info.params: {} the selected envelope's settings, or with none selected the defaults new envelopes get → {id: n|null, type: warp|mesh|topObject, style, bend, h, v, horizontal, rows, cols, fidelity, antiAlias, preserveShape: clippingMask|transparency, distortAppearance, distortLinearGradients, distortPatternFills, editing}
cmd:object.envelope.info.desc: Report an envelope's type, warp style, mesh size and distortion settings.

cmd:object.envelope.resetWithMesh.label: Reset with Mesh…
cmd:object.envelope.resetWithMesh.params: {rows?: 1..50, cols?: 1..50 (unset: a mesh envelope's own, else 4), maintainShape?: bool (true: the mesh follows the current envelope shape; false: a flat grid over the content)} make the selected envelopes mesh envelopes, keeping their content
cmd:object.envelope.resetWithMesh.desc: Turn existing envelopes into mesh envelopes, keeping their content.

cmd:object.envelope.resetWithWarp.label: Reset with Warp…
cmd:object.envelope.resetWithWarp.params: {style?, bend?, h?, v?, horizontal? | orientation? (as makeWithWarp; unset: the envelope's current warp, else arc 50 %)} make the selected envelopes warp envelopes, keeping their content
cmd:object.envelope.resetWithWarp.desc: Turn existing envelopes into warp envelopes with a preset style, keeping content.

cmd:object.maskImage.label: Mask
cmd:object.maskImage.params: {} clip the selected image with a rectangle around it (its own outline, rotated with it) and select that clipping path, whose handles then crop it; one undo step → {id: the clip group, path: the clipping path}
cmd:object.maskImage.desc: Crop a placed image with a rectangular clipping mask matching its outline.

cmd:object.puppetWarp.pins.label: Puppet Warp Pins
cmd:object.puppetWarp.pins.params: {id?|ids? (default: selection), expand?: pt} → {ids, pins, moved, angles, expand, rest: true, auto} the Puppet Warp pins on the art: pins = where each sits on the shape they started from, moved = where it is now, angles = the turn it holds (deg, null = free); auto: none placed yet (the tool's automatic pins: the centre and the end of each limb). Change moved/angles (or add/remove pins) and pass it back to object.puppetWarp
cmd:object.puppetWarp.pins.desc: Report the Puppet Warp pins on the art: rest spots, current spots and turns.

cmd:object.slice.clipToArtboard.label: Clip to Artboard
cmd:object.slice.clipToArtboard.params: {on?: bool} toggle (or set) Clip to Artboard: on, slices are clipped to the artboards and auto slices fill them; off, auto slices cover the art and the slices → {on}
cmd:object.slice.clipToArtboard.desc: Toggle whether slices are clipped to the artboards with auto slices filling them.

cmd:object.slice.combine.label: Combine Slices
cmd:object.slice.combine.params: {} replace the two or more selected slices with one user slice over their bounds (the first one's options; object slices are released) → {id}
cmd:object.slice.combine.desc: Merge selected slices into one slice spanning their bounds.

cmd:object.slice.create.label: Create Slice
cmd:object.slice.create.params: {x, y, width, height} a user slice over that rectangle, selected (the Slice tool's drag) → {id}
cmd:object.slice.create.desc: Draw a new user slice over a rectangle for web export.

cmd:object.slice.delete.label: Delete Slices
cmd:object.slice.delete.params: {slices?: [id…] (default: the selected slices)} delete the user slices and release the object slices (their objects stay) → {count}
cmd:object.slice.delete.desc: Delete chosen user slices and release object slices, keeping their objects.

cmd:object.slice.deleteAll.label: Delete All
cmd:object.slice.deleteAll.params: {} delete every user slice and release every object slice → {count}
cmd:object.slice.deleteAll.desc: Delete every user slice and release every object slice.

cmd:object.slice.divide.label: Divide Slices…
cmd:object.slice.divide.params: {rows?: slices down, rowHeight?: pt per slice, columns?: slices across, columnWidth?: pt per slice} cut each selected slice into a grid of user slices (evenly by count, or by size with a smaller last one; an object slice is released); the pieces are selected → {ids}
cmd:object.slice.divide.desc: Cut selected slices into a grid of smaller slices by count or size.

cmd:object.slice.duplicate.label: Duplicate Slice
cmd:object.slice.duplicate.params: {dx?: pt (default 10), dy?: pt (default 10)} copy the selected slices as user slices with their options, offset by dx, dy; the copies are selected → {ids}
cmd:object.slice.duplicate.desc: Copy selected slices, offset slightly, with their options.

cmd:object.slice.fromGuides.label: Create from Guides
cmd:object.slice.fromGuides.params: {} replace the user slices with the grid the ruler guides cut the artboards into (two vertical and two horizontal guides give 9) → {ids}
cmd:object.slice.fromGuides.desc: Replace user slices with the grid that the ruler guides cut the artboards into.

cmd:object.slice.fromSelection.label: Create from Selection
cmd:object.slice.fromSelection.params: {ids?} a user slice over the visual bounds of the selected objects (or ids), selected → {id}
cmd:object.slice.fromSelection.desc: Make a user slice covering the selected objects' bounds.

cmd:object.slice.make.label: Make
cmd:object.slice.make.params: {ids?} make each selected object (or ids) an object slice: its slice follows the object's bounds → {ids: the new object slices}
cmd:object.slice.make.desc: Turn each selected object into an object slice that follows its bounds.

cmd:object.slice.move.label: Move Slices
cmd:object.slice.move.params: {slices?: [id…] (default: the selected slices), dx, dy} move the slices: user slices move, object slices move their objects → {ids}
cmd:object.slice.move.desc: Move slices by an offset; object slices carry their objects along.

cmd:object.slice.options.label: Slice Options…
cmd:object.slice.options.params: {kind?: "image"|"noImage"|"htmlText" (object slices of type only), name?, url?, target?, message?, alt?: (image), text?: cell text, HTML allowed (noImage), background?: ""|"matte"|"#rrggbb", hAlign?: "default"|"left"|"center"|"right", vAlign?: "default"|"top"|"middle"|"baseline"|"bottom"} set the selected slices' options as one undo step; no options: read them → the first slice's {kind, name, url, target, message, alt, text, background, hAlign, vAlign, htmlText: whether HTML Text applies}
cmd:object.slice.options.desc: Set a slice's name, link URL, target and background for web export.

cmd:object.slice.release.label: Release
cmd:object.slice.release.params: {} release the selected slices: an object slice leaves its object as it was, a user slice becomes an unpainted rectangle; the objects end up selected → {ids}
cmd:object.slice.release.desc: Release slices: object slices leave their objects, user slices become plain rectangles.

cmd:object.slice.select.label: Select Slices
cmd:object.slice.select.params: {slices?: [id…] (user slice ids or ids of objects with an object slice; none: deselect the slices), toggle?: bool (Shift: add the unselected ones, drop the selected ones)} select slices as the Slice Selection tool does; the objects are deselected → {selected: [id…]}
cmd:object.slice.select.desc: Select slices like the Slice Selection tool, adding or toggling.

cmd:object.slice.setRect.label: Set Slice Rectangle
cmd:object.slice.setRect.params: {id: user slice, x, y, width, height} move or resize a user slice (an object slice follows its object) → {id}
cmd:object.slice.setRect.desc: Move or resize a user slice to exact coordinates and size.

cmd:object.vectorHalftone.label: Vector Halftone…
cmd:object.vectorHalftone.params: {shape?: "circle"|"ellipse"|"square"|"diamond"|"line" (circle), frequency?: lines per inch 1–300 (20), angle?: deg (45; CMYK: the black screen's, cyan −30°, magenta +30°, yellow −45° from it), mode?: "mono"|"cmyk" (mono), color?: mono dot colour ("#000000"), invert?: bool (dots for light tones), clip?: true (clip the dots to the art's outline), keepOriginal?: false} the selection as vector halftone dots sized by its tone, a group of one path per screen (CMYK screens multiply), as one undo step → {id, dots}
cmd:object.vectorHalftone.desc: Turn artwork into vector halftone dots or lines in mono or CMYK.

cmd:path.lineCut.label: Line Cut
cmd:path.lineCut.params: {from: [x,y], to: [x,y]} split the selected paths and compound paths along the line through both points, extended across the art: filled shapes become their pieces on each side (holes kept), open paths split where they cross; as one undo step → {ids, removed: 0}
cmd:path.lineCut.desc: Split selected paths along a straight line through two points.

cmd:path.mirrorCut.label: Mirror & Cut
cmd:path.mirrorCut.params: {axis?: "vertical"|"horizontal"|"free" (vertical), from?: [x,y], to?: [x,y] (free: the axis through both; vertical/horizontal: the axis through `from`, default the selection's centre), keep?: "left"|"right"|"top"|"bottom" (the side kept; default left, or top for a horizontal-ish axis)} cut the selected paths and compound paths at the axis, reflect the kept half across it and join both halves into one closed shape (open paths are joined where they meet the axis); art wholly on the other side is deleted, as one undo step → {ids, removed}
cmd:path.mirrorCut.desc: Mirror artwork across an axis and cut away one side.

cmd:path.rectCut.label: Rectangle Cut
cmd:path.rectCut.params: {rect: [x, y, width, height]} or {from: [x,y], to: [x,y]} (opposite corners) crop the selected paths and compound paths to the rectangle as real geometry (not a clipping mask): filled shapes are intersected with it, open paths keep their parts inside, art wholly outside is deleted; as one undo step → {ids, removed}
cmd:path.rectCut.desc: Crop selected paths to a rectangle as real geometry, not a clipping mask.

cmd:path.removeAnchors.label: Remove Anchor Points
cmd:path.removeAnchors.params: {} remove the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curve round each → {removedObjects}
cmd:path.removeAnchors.desc: Remove selected anchors without opening the path, refitting the curve around each.

cmd:pdf.preset.delete.label: Delete PDF Preset
cmd:pdf.preset.delete.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}
cmd:pdf.preset.delete.desc: Delete a saved PDF preset, leaving built-in ones intact.

cmd:pdf.preset.export.label: Export PDF Presets
cmd:pdf.preset.export.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcpdfpresets file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}
cmd:pdf.preset.export.desc: Save PDF presets to a file for sharing or backup.

cmd:pdf.preset.import.label: Import PDF Presets
cmd:pdf.preset.import.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcpdfpresets file (as pdf.preset.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}
cmd:pdf.preset.import.desc: Add PDF presets from a shared presets file.

cmd:pdf.preset.list.label: PDF Presets
cmd:pdf.preset.list.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, supported (the writer produces its standard), description, settings (as document.pdfSettings)}]} the built-in presets (VectorCraft Default first), then the saved ones; any of these names works as `preset` wherever PDF options are taken
cmd:pdf.preset.list.desc: List built-in and saved PDF presets with their settings.

cmd:pdf.preset.save.label: Save PDF Preset
cmd:pdf.preset.save.params: {name?: (default: a new "PDF Preset N"), newName?: rename it, description?, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else VectorCraft Default), …document.exportPdf options} create or change a saved preset (built-in presets are read-only; passwords are never stored) → {name, created, settings}
cmd:pdf.preset.save.desc: Create or update a saved PDF preset with custom export settings.

cmd:perspective.editText.label: Edit Text
cmd:perspective.editText.params: {id? (default: the selected type)} Object › Perspective › Edit Text: show type in perspective flat where it is drawn, in isolation mode, to edit it (text.* commands, the Type tool); exiting isolation (object.exitIsolation, Esc) projects it again → {id}
cmd:perspective.editText.desc: Edit perspective type flat in isolation mode, reprojecting it when done.

cmd:perspective.grid.define.label: Define Perspective Grid
cmd:perspective.grid.define.params: {name?: preset name ("" = custom), kind?: 1|2|3, units?: unit name (points, pixels, inches, centimeters, millimeters…), scale?: [artboard, real world], gridline?: gridline every, angle?: viewing angle (0–90°), distance?: viewing distance, horizonHeight?: above the ground level, thirdVp?: [x right, y up] from the centre of vision (3-point), leftColor?, rightColor?, groundColor?: "#rrggbb", opacity?: 0–100} lengths are real-world lengths in `units` at `scale`; missing fields keep the grid's (see perspective.grid.get define). Only what changes changes: a new type, angle or distance moves the vanishing points around the station point. One undo step → the new define fields
cmd:perspective.grid.define.desc: Define the perspective grid: kind, scale, viewing angle, distance and horizon.

cmd:perspective.grid.get.label: Perspective Grid
cmd:perspective.grid.get.params: {} → {grid: the model (as perspective.grid.set takes it), define: the Define Grid fields (as perspective.grid.define takes them), station: {x, y, distance} (the viewer: centre of vision on the horizon, distance to the picture plane, pt), defined: false while the document uses the default grid}
cmd:perspective.grid.get.desc: Report the document's perspective grid definition and viewer station.

cmd:perspective.grid.lock.label: Lock Grid
cmd:perspective.grid.lock.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) View › Perspective Grid › Lock Grid: the grid's widgets can't be dragged (the Plane Switching Widget still works). View state: not an undo step → {on}
cmd:perspective.grid.lock.desc: Lock the perspective grid so its widgets cannot be dragged.

cmd:perspective.grid.lockStation.label: Lock Station Point
cmd:perspective.grid.lockStation.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) dragging one vanishing point moves the other around the station point (the viewing angle turns, the viewer stays). View state: not an undo step → {on}
cmd:perspective.grid.lockStation.desc: Lock the viewer so dragging one vanishing point turns the viewing angle instead.

cmd:perspective.grid.rulers.label: Show Rulers
cmd:perspective.grid.rulers.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) a ruler up the line where the planes meet, in the grid's units at its scale. View state: not an undo step → {on}
cmd:perspective.grid.rulers.desc: Show a ruler along the plane intersection in the grid's units.

cmd:perspective.grid.snap.label: Snap to Grid
cmd:perspective.grid.snap.params: {on?: bool} (no param toggles) art drawn or moved in perspective lands on gridlines within a quarter cell (on by default). View state: not an undo step → {on}
cmd:perspective.grid.snap.desc: Snap art drawn or moved in perspective onto the gridlines.

cmd:perspective.nudge.label: Nudge in Perspective
cmd:perspective.nudge.params: {dx, dy: arrow direction (-1, 0 or 1), big?: bool (×10), copy?: bool} move the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool → {ids}
cmd:perspective.nudge.desc: Nudge the selection along a perspective plane with arrow-key steps.

cmd:perspective.plane.matchObject.label: Move Plane to Match Object
cmd:perspective.plane.matchObject.params: {id? (default: the first selected object)} move the plane the object is attached to onto the object and make it the active plane → {plane, offset}
cmd:perspective.plane.matchObject.desc: Move a perspective plane onto an object and make it the active plane.

cmd:perspective.plane.move.label: Move Plane
cmd:perspective.plane.move.params: {plane?: left|right|ground (default: the active plane), offset?: pt (where along its normal; 0 is its place in the grid's definition) | by?: pt, objects?: none|move|copy (default none: the objects on the plane stay; move: they move with it, as Shift-dragging a plane widget does; copy: copies of them do, as Alt-dragging does)} → {plane, offset, ids}
cmd:perspective.plane.move.desc: Move a perspective plane along its normal, optionally carrying or copying its objects.

cmd:perspective.presets.delete.label: Delete Perspective Grid Preset
cmd:perspective.presets.delete.params: {name} delete a saved preset (built-in ones stay) → {deleted: name}
cmd:perspective.presets.delete.desc: Delete a saved perspective grid preset, keeping built-in ones.

cmd:perspective.presets.export.label: Export Perspective Grid Presets
cmd:perspective.presets.export.params: {names?: [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcperspective file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}
cmd:perspective.presets.export.desc: Save perspective grid presets to a shareable file.

cmd:perspective.presets.import.label: Import Perspective Grid Presets
cmd:perspective.presets.import.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcperspective file (as perspective.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}
cmd:perspective.presets.import.desc: Add perspective grid presets from a shared file.

cmd:perspective.presets.list.label: Perspective Grid Presets
cmd:perspective.presets.list.params: {} → {presets: [{builtIn, name, kind, …the perspective.grid.define fields}]} the built-in views (fitted to the first artboard, protected) first, then the saved presets
cmd:perspective.presets.list.desc: List built-in and saved perspective grid presets with their definitions.

cmd:perspective.presets.save.label: Save Perspective Grid Preset
cmd:perspective.presets.save.params: {name?: (default: a new "Perspective Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else the document's grid), …the perspective.grid.define fields (over it)} create or change a saved preset (Save Grid as Preset: just `name`); built-in ones are protected → {name, created, definition}
cmd:perspective.presets.save.desc: Save the current perspective grid as a named preset.

cmd:perspective.transform.label: Transform in Perspective
cmd:perspective.transform.params: {ids?, matrix: [a,b,c,d,e,f] (affine map in plane coordinates, points: u along the plane, v up or away), depth?: pt to move along the plane's normal (default 0), copy?: bool, plane?} transform objects within their own planes (Perspective Selection tool handles; unattached objects attach to `plane`/the active plane first); Transform Again repeats it → {ids}
cmd:perspective.transform.desc: Transform objects inside their perspective planes with an affine matrix.

cmd:perspective.widget.options.label: Perspective Grid Options
cmd:perspective.widget.options.params: {show?: bool, position?: topLeft|topRight|bottomLeft|bottomRight} the Plane Switching Widget: shown or not, and the corner of the document window it stays in (kept with the preferences; no params reads them) → {show, position}
cmd:perspective.widget.options.desc: Show or hide the plane switching widget and choose its window corner.

cmd:plugin.dialog.label: Plug-in…
cmd:plugin.dialog.params: {id: an object filter plug-in (plugin.list), params?: {…}} Object › Plug-ins: run the filter at once when it takes no parameters or params are given (plugin.run), else open its dialog (dialog `plugin`: a field per parameter, `__plugin` the id, live preview; OK runs plugin.run as one undo step)
cmd:plugin.dialog.desc: Run a plug-in filter at once or open its options dialog.

cmd:plugin.info.label: Plug-in Info
cmd:plugin.info.params: {id} → plugin.list's entry plus {manifest, defaults, lastError (a live effect's last failure, null)}
cmd:plugin.info.desc: Report a plug-in's details, parameters and last error.

cmd:plugin.install.label: Install Plug-in
cmd:plugin.install.params: {path: a .wasm file (desktop) | dataBase64: the module (+ name?: shown as its source), replace?: bool (true: a plug-in with the same id is replaced)} validate and install a WebAssembly plug-in for this session → its plugin.list entry
cmd:plugin.install.desc: Validate and install a WebAssembly plug-in for this session.

cmd:plugin.list.label: List Plug-ins
cmd:plugin.list.params: {} → {plugins: [{id, name, version, kind: "filter"|"effect", author, description, params (doc), paramsSchema, effect? (the effect id of a live effect: plugin.<id>), size, source}], folder: the Additional Plug-ins Folder load report {folder, loaded, failed: [{file, error}]} | null}
cmd:plugin.list.desc: List installed plug-ins with version, author, parameters and effect ids.

cmd:plugin.reload.label: Reload Plug-ins
cmd:plugin.reload.params: {path?: a folder (default: the Additional Plug-ins Folder preference)} install every *.wasm in it (desktop; a bad module is reported and skipped) → {folder, loaded: [id], failed: [{file, error}]}
cmd:plugin.reload.desc: Load every WebAssembly plug-in from the additional plug-ins folder again.

cmd:plugin.remove.label: Remove Plug-in
cmd:plugin.remove.params: {id} uninstall a plug-in (its live effects then leave the geometry as it is) → {removed}
cmd:plugin.remove.desc: Uninstall a plug-in from this session.

cmd:plugin.run.label: Run Plug-in
cmd:plugin.run.params: {id, params?: {…} (the plug-in's parameters; or give them as top-level keys; missing ones take their defaults, see plugin.info), ids?: [..] (default: the selection)} run an object filter on the selected paths and compound paths (inside selected groups and layers too; hidden, locked, guide and clipping paths are left out): it may change, delete or add objects, as one undo step; the result is selected. With nothing selected it gets no objects (generators add theirs to the current layer) → {plugin, ids}
cmd:plugin.run.desc: Run a plug-in filter on the selected artwork with given parameters.

cmd:print.presets.delete.label: Delete Print Preset
cmd:print.presets.delete.params: {name} delete a saved preset ([Default] stays) → {deleted: name}
cmd:print.presets.delete.desc: Delete a saved print preset, keeping the default.

cmd:print.presets.export.label: Export Print Presets
cmd:print.presets.export.params: {names?: [preset names, [Default] too] (default: every saved preset), path?} write the presets as a .vcprintpresets file (JSON) → {path, count}; without path → {data: the file's text, count}
cmd:print.presets.export.desc: Save print presets to a shareable file.

cmd:print.presets.import.label: Import Print Presets
cmd:print.presets.import.params: {path? | data?: file text | dataBase64?, replace?: false (replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number)} add the presets of a .vcprintpresets file (as print.presets.export writes) to the saved ones → {imported: [names]}
cmd:print.presets.import.desc: Add print presets from a shared file.

cmd:print.presets.list.label: Print Presets
cmd:print.presets.list.params: {} → {presets: [{name, builtIn, settings (as print.setup's), changed: [{option, value}] (how it differs from [Default])}]} [Default] (the default print settings, protected) first, then the saved presets
cmd:print.presets.list.desc: List the default and saved print presets with their settings.

cmd:print.presets.save.label: Save Print Preset
cmd:print.presets.save.params: {name?: (default: a new "Print Preset N"), newName?: rename it, preset?: the preset to start from (default: the saved preset `name`, else [Default]), settings?: {…print.setup settings} (over it)} create or change a saved preset ([Default] is protected) → {name, created, settings}
cmd:print.presets.save.desc: Create or update a saved print preset from current print settings.

cmd:print.preview.label: Print Preview
cmd:print.preview.params: {settings?: {…print.setup settings} (over the document's)} → {pages (copies included), sheets: [{artboard (0-based; null with artboards ignored), tile? (1-based), ink? (separations), width, height (pt, the page), orientation, scale: [width %, height %], transform: [a, b, c, d, e, f] (document space → the page, pt, y down), area: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the document region the page prints), trim: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the artboard on the page)}] (one copy, in order), tiles: [{artboard, columns, rows, printed: [1-based tiles], tiles: [[x0, y0, x1, y1]…] (document space)}], inks: [{name, spot, print, frequency, angle}] (separations), warnings (art larger than the imageable area, options not applied yet…), settings} without printing
cmd:print.preview.desc: Show how the pages will print: sheets, tiles, scaling and separations.

cmd:print.printerSetup.label: Printer Setup…
cmd:print.printerSetup.params: {printer?} open the system's settings of the printer (the Print dialog's Setup…; desktop)
cmd:print.printerSetup.desc: Open the operating system's settings for a printer.

cmd:print.printers.label: Printers
cmd:print.printers.params: {} → {printers: [{name, default}] (the system's printers), service (printing is available; else Print saves a PDF), setup (print.printerSetup can open the printer settings)}
cmd:print.printers.desc: List the system's printers and whether printing is available.

cmd:print.setup.label: Print Setup
cmd:print.setup.params: {settings?: {copies: 1 (1–999), collate: true, reverse, artboards: all|range|ignore (all the art as one page), range: "1-3, 5" (1-based, with artboards: range), skipBlank (leave out artboards with no art that prints), media: letter|legal|tabloid|a3|a4|a5|b4|b5|custom, width, height (custom paper, 72–14400 pt), orientation: portrait|landscape|portraitFlipped|landscapeFlipped, autoRotate: true (turn the paper to each artboard; orientation ignored), transverse (the page a quarter turn on the paper), printLayers: visiblePrintable|visible|all (template layers never print), placement: {origin: topLeft|top|topRight|left|center|right|bottomLeft|bottom|bottomRight (the point of the printed area, the artboard with its bleed and marks, on the same point of the imageable area), x, y (pt, right and down)}, scaling: none|fit|custom|tileFull|tileImageable, scale: {width: 100, height: 100} (% with custom and tiling), overlap: 0 (pt between tiles), tileRange: "" (1-based tiles across then down; empty: all), margin: 0 (pt the device can't print around the paper: the imageable area is inside it), marks: {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman|japanese, weight: 0.25, offset: 6} (as document.exportPdf, at the paper's scale; page information adds the tile and the ink), bleed: {useDocument: true (the document's bleed, document.setup), top, bottom, left, right} (pt), output: {mode: composite|separations (one grey page per ink that prints), emulsion: up|down (down mirrors), image: positive|negative, spotsToProcess, inks: [{name: "Cyan"|…|a spot swatch, print: true, frequency (lpi, default 60), angle (default C 15, M 75, Y 0, K 45, spots 45)}]}, graphics: {autoFlatness: true, flatness: 1 (0.2–100), fonts: none|subset|complete}, color: {intent: perceptual|relativeColorimetric|saturation|absoluteColorimetric, preserveNumbers: true (CMYK colours keep their values), profile: "" (the printer profile, an RGB or CMYK one: composite PDF colours are converted to it with the intent, separations separate with a CMYK one; empty: as they are)}, advanced: {printAsBitmap (composite pages print as one image each, at the document's raster effects resolution), overprints: preserve|discard|simulate (composite output; preserve writes them to overprint (/OP), simulate prints them as Overprint Preview shows them; separations always keep them), flattenerPreset: "" (a flattener preset, built-in or saved: transparency is flattened before printing; empty: it prints live; PostScript defaults to medium)}, tileOrigin: {placed: false, x, y} (where the Print Tiling tool put the pages: print.tiling.set)}} store the print settings with the document, over the ones it has (null keeps a value), as one undo step; no settings → {settings} (the current ones, defaults if never set up)
cmd:print.setup.desc: Set copies, paper, scaling, tiling and colour separations for printing.

cmd:print.tiling.label: Print Tiling Pages
cmd:print.tiling.params: {settings?: {…print.setup settings} (over the document's)} the pages as View → Show Print Tiling draws them, from print.preview's layout → {tileOrigin, pages: [{artboard (0-based; null with artboards ignored), number (1-based tile across then down, or page), printed (tiles outside tileRange don't), page: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (the paper's edge), imageable: [x0, y0, x1, y1] (inside the unprintable margin)}] (document space; every tile when tiling, else each page once)}
cmd:print.tiling.desc: Show how the art divides across printed pages for tiling.

cmd:print.tiling.set.label: Print Tiling
cmd:print.tiling.set.params: {origin: [x, y] (document point: the top-left corner of the first page's imageable area), artboard? (0-based: the artboard it is measured from; default the printed artboard containing origin, else the first; ignored with artboards: ignore)} | {reset: true} place the printed pages as the Print Tiling tool does, saved with the print settings (tileOrigin: {placed, x, y}, from the artboard's top-left corner; it replaces the placement, and tiles start there), as one undo step; reset → the placement places them again → {tileOrigin}
cmd:print.tiling.set.desc: Position the print tiling origin that decides where pages fall on the art.

cmd:ui.dxfOptionsDialog.label: DXF Options Dialog

cmd:ui.dxfOptionsDialog.desc: Open the DXF Options dialog to set and save a DXF export.

cmd:ui.epsOptionsDialog.label: EPS Options Dialog

cmd:ui.epsOptionsDialog.desc: Open the EPS Options dialog to set and save an EPS export.

cmd:ui.fileInfoDialog.label: File Info Dialog

cmd:ui.fileInfoDialog.desc: Open the File Info dialog to edit title, author, keywords and copyright.

cmd:ui.installPlugin.label: Install Plug-in…

cmd:webExport.settings.label: Save for Web Settings
cmd:webExport.settings.params: {reset?: false, preset?, …the settings of document.exportForWeb} remember settings for the Save for Web dialog (it opens on them): the keys given change the remembered ones, a preset replaces them, reset goes back to the defaults; {} reads them → {settings}
cmd:webExport.settings.desc: Remember Save for Web settings so the dialog opens with them.

cmd:window.collapseDock.label: Collapse Panels to Icons
cmd:window.collapseDock.params: {collapsed?: bool} collapse the dock's Properties | Layers | Libraries group to icons (true), expand it (false) or toggle (omitted), as the double arrow at the top of the dock does; returns the new state
cmd:window.collapseDock.desc: Collapse the panel dock to icons or expand it again.

cmd:window.floatTools.label: Float Tool Group
cmd:window.floatTools.params: {tool: id, floating?: bool} float the toolbar group holding `tool` (in the current Basic or Advanced layout) as its own strip of tool buttons (true), put it back in the toolbar (false) or toggle (omitted), as dragging or clicking a flyout's tear-off bar and the strip's × do; returns the new state
cmd:window.floatTools.desc: Float a toolbar group as its own strip or dock it back.

cmd:window.taskBar.pin.label: Pin Bar Position
cmd:window.taskBar.pin.params: {pinned?: bool} keep the Contextual Task Bar where it is instead of following the selection (true), let it follow the selection again from where it is (false) or toggle (omitted), as the bar's More Options menu does; returns the new state
cmd:window.taskBar.pin.desc: Pin the contextual task bar in place or let it follow the selection again.

cmd:window.taskBar.reset.label: Reset Bar Position
cmd:window.taskBar.reset.params: {} unpin the Contextual Task Bar and put it back under the selection
cmd:window.taskBar.reset.desc: Unpin the contextual task bar and move it back under the selection.
